items.function_short: Lets the gut absorb calcium and phosphate so that bone can mineralise properly.
items.function_full: Cholecalciferol is hydroxylated in the liver to 25-hydroxyvitamin D, the circulating storage form measured on a blood test, and then in the kidney to 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D (calcitriol), a steroid hormone acting through the nuclear vitamin D receptor. Calcitriol drives active intestinal absorption of calcium and phosphate, suppresses parathyroid hormone, and maintains the calcium-phosphate product that osteoblasts need to mineralise newly laid osteoid. Vitamin D receptors are present in immune cells, muscle and many other tissues, but the only role with an established human requirement is the calcium and bone axis. Skin synthesis from UVB normally supplies most of it, which is why dietary requirement figures depend heavily on latitude, season and sun exposure.
items.deficiency_name: Rickets in growing children, osteomalacia in adults. Severe infant deficiency also causes hypocalcaemic seizures and dilated cardiomyopathy.
items.deficiency_early: Serum 25(OH)D falls first, then parathyroid hormone rises (secondary hyperparathyroidism) while serum calcium is still normal or low-normal. At this stage a person notices little or nothing: vague aching in the hips, ribs and shins, and proximal muscle weakness showing up as difficulty rising from a low chair or climbing stairs. A blood test shows low 25(OH)D, raised PTH and often raised alkaline phosphatase before any X-ray change.
items.deficiency_severe: In children, growth plates fail to mineralise: bowed legs or knock knees, widened wrists and ankles, the rachitic rosary at the costochondral junctions, delayed walking, poor growth and fractures. Infants can present first with hypocalcaemic tetany, seizures or dilated cardiomyopathy, which can be fatal. In adults, unmineralised osteoid accumulates as osteomalacia, giving bone pain, proximal myopathy with a waddling gait, and Looser zones (pseudofractures) that progress to complete fractures of the pubic rami, femoral neck or ribs.
items.reversibility_note: Biochemistry, bone pain, myopathy, hypocalcaemic seizures and the radiological signs of active rickets correct completely with vitamin D plus adequate calcium, usually over weeks to a few months. Skeletal deformity already established in long-standing rickets often persists, and marked bowing, rachitic dwarfism or pelvic deformity may need surgical correction.
items.at_risk: People with little effective sun exposure: housebound or institutionalised older adults, those who cover the skin fully, and anyone living at high latitude through winter. Darker skin at high latitude (more melanin means less UVB synthesis). Exclusively breastfed infants not given a supplement, since breast milk is low in vitamin D. Obesity (sequestration in adipose tissue). Fat malabsorption from coeliac disease, cystic fibrosis, cholestasis or bariatric surgery. Chronic kidney or liver disease, and long-term anticonvulsant or glucocorticoid therapy.
items.prevalence: NHANES 2011-2014: 5.0% of the US population aged 1 year and over had serum 25(OH)D below 30 nmol/L (at risk of deficiency) and 18.3% fell between 30 and 49.9 nmol/L; the below-30 figure was 17.5% in non-Hispanic Black participants against 2.1% in non-Hispanic White participants (PMID 31076739). Clinical nutritional rickets is uncommon in high-income countries but has not disappeared, and remains common in parts of the Middle East, Africa and South Asia (PMID 26741135).
items.source: PMID 31076739 (Herrick KA et al., Am J Clin Nutr 2019, Vitamin D status in the United States 2011-2014); PMID 26741135 (Munns CF et al., Horm Res Paediatr 2016;85(2):83-106, Global Consensus Recommendations on Prevention and Management of Nutritional Rickets; co-published in J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2016;101(2):394-415, which is PMID 26745253)

items.supplement: Vitamin E at or above 400 IU/d
items.function_short: The body's main fat-soluble antioxidant, protecting cell membranes and nerves from oxidative damage.
items.function_full: Alpha-tocopherol is the only form of vitamin E the body retains. After absorption, hepatic alpha-tocopherol transfer protein (TTPA) selectively loads alpha-tocopherol onto VLDL for export to tissues, while the other tocopherols and the tocotrienols are metabolised and excreted. Its established function is to break the chain reaction of lipid peroxidation in the polyunsaturated fatty acids of cell membranes and lipoproteins, donating a hydrogen atom to lipid peroxyl radicals and then being regenerated by ascorbate. The tissues that suffer first without it are peripheral nerve axons, the posterior columns and cerebellum, the retina, and the erythrocyte membrane. Converting the dose properly (1 mg alpha-tocopherol = 1.49 IU natural-source RRR, 2.22 IU synthetic all-rac), 400 IU is 268 mg of natural-source or 180 mg of synthetic alpha-tocopherol, roughly 12 to 18 times the adult RDA of 15 mg/d depending on which form the product uses, so at that level it is being used pharmacologically rather than to correct any dietary shortfall.
items.deficiency_name: No classic single-name disease. The recognised syndrome is vitamin E deficiency ataxia, a spinocerebellar degeneration with peripheral neuropathy and pigmentary retinopathy; in preterm infants it presents as haemolytic anaemia of prematurity. Ataxia with isolated vitamin E deficiency (AVED) produces the same clinical picture but is an inherited TTPA gene defect, not a dietary deficiency.
items.deficiency_early: Plasma alpha-tocopherol below roughly 12 micromol/L, or a low tocopherol-to-total-lipid ratio, precedes symptoms by months to years and is the practical marker. The first clinical signs are loss of ankle reflexes and reduced vibration and joint position sense in the feet, sometimes with unsteady walking in the dark. In preterm infants, a haemolytic anaemia with raised reticulocytes.
items.deficiency_severe: Untreated, it progresses to a combined spinocerebellar and sensory picture: ataxia from posterior column degeneration, dysarthria, ophthalmoplegia, head titubation, proximal weakness, and pigmentary retinopathy with declining visual acuity. The endpoint is a person who can no longer walk unaided, with fixed sensory ataxia and neuropathy.
items.reversibility_note: High-dose repletion reliably halts progression, and when started early (within roughly a year of symptom onset, or before symptoms in a child with known malabsorption) much of the neuropathy recovers. Long-standing posterior column and cerebellar degeneration and established retinopathy usually do not fully resolve, so treatment prevents more than it restores.
items.at_risk: Almost exclusively people who cannot absorb fat: cystic fibrosis, cholestatic liver disease and biliary atresia, short bowel syndrome, chronic pancreatitis, abetalipoproteinaemia and homozygous hypobetalipoproteinaemia. Preterm and very low birth weight infants. Separately, people with the inherited TTPA defect (AVED), which is a genetic transport disorder rather than a consequence of diet. In an adult with normal fat absorption, eating too little vitamin E essentially does not produce clinical deficiency. At the 400 IU/d dose this entry names, the established direction of effect is harm rather than repletion: in SELECT, 400 IU/d of alpha-tocopherol raised prostate cancer incidence in healthy men (HR 1.17, 99% CI 1.004-1.36; PMID 21990298).
items.prevalence: NOT ESTABLISHED for frank clinical deficiency, which is rare enough in the general population that no meaningful prevalence figure exists. The widely quoted claim that over 90% of Americans fail to meet the estimated average requirement for alpha-tocopherol is an intake statistic, not a deficiency rate, and no corresponding burden of neurological disease accompanies it (doi:10.3945/an.114.006254). Biochemical deficiency is common in untreated cystic fibrosis and cholestatic liver disease.
items.source: doi:10.3945/an.114.006254 (Traber MG, Adv Nutr 2014, Vitamin E inadequacy in humans: causes and consequences); PMID 6308196 (Sokol RJ et al., J Pediatr 1983;103:197-204, vitamin E deficiency during chronic childhood cholestasis with sural nerve axonopathy, the malabsorptive syndrome this entry classifies); PMID 15681888 (Jayaram S et al., Indian J Med Sci 2005, a single case report of AVED, cited only for the inherited TTPA picture described under deficiency_name and for its partial response to replacement, not as evidence for acquired deficiency); PMID 21990298 (Klein EA et al., JAMA 2011;306:1549-56, SELECT); PMID 35727271 (USPSTF Recommendation Statement, JAMA 2022, D recommendation against vitamin E for CVD or cancer prevention)

items.supplement: Preformed vitamin A at or above 10,000 IU
items.function_short: Makes the eye's dim-light pigment and keeps skin, gut and airway linings healthy.
items.function_full: Retinol is oxidised to 11-cis-retinal, which binds opsin to form rhodopsin, the photopigment of the rod cells that makes vision in dim light possible. By a separate route it is oxidised to all-trans and 9-cis retinoic acid, ligands for the nuclear RAR and RXR receptors, which regulate transcription of genes controlling epithelial differentiation (goblet cells and mucin production in the conjunctiva, cornea, respiratory tract and gut), embryonic patterning, haematopoiesis, and both innate and adaptive immunity including gut-homing of T lymphocytes. Preformed retinol from liver, dairy, eggs and supplements is absorbed efficiently and stored in hepatic stellate cells, which buffer plasma concentrations for months. 10,000 IU is about 3,000 micrograms retinol activity equivalents, roughly four times the adult RDA and at the tolerable upper intake level, so at this dose the clinically relevant question is excess rather than shortfall.
items.deficiency_name: Xerophthalmia, the spectrum running from night blindness (nyctalopia) through conjunctival and corneal xerosis to keratomalacia.
items.deficiency_early: Impaired dark adaptation, then frank night blindness: trouble seeing after dusk or in a dimly lit room, which in a small child shows as reluctance to move about after dark. Conjunctival xerosis and Bitot spots, foamy grey triangular patches of keratinised conjunctiva, follow. Increased severity and duration of measles, diarrhoea and respiratory infection often precede any eye sign. Serum retinol below 0.70 micromol/L is the biochemical marker, though it falls only once liver stores are largely gone.
items.deficiency_severe: Corneal xerosis progresses to punctate keratopathy, then corneal ulceration, then keratomalacia, in which the corneal stroma liquefies over a few days and frequently perforates. The eye is structurally destroyed and blindness is permanent. Deficiency also substantially raises child mortality from measles, diarrhoeal disease and respiratory infection, and roughly half of the children who go blind from it die within twelve months.
items.reversibility_note: Night blindness, conjunctival xerosis and Bitot spots reverse within days to weeks of high-dose retinol. Once the cornea ulcerates or melts, the loss is structural and permanent, and vitamin A deficiency remains a leading cause of preventable childhood blindness worldwide. The window between the fully reversible and the irreversible stage can be only a few days in a sick, depleted child, which is why treatment is given on clinical suspicion without waiting for a retinol assay.
items.at_risk: Preschool children and pregnant and lactating women in low-income settings whose diets contain little animal-source food or provitamin A vegetables, particularly where measles and diarrhoeal disease are common. In high-income countries deficiency is rare and almost always secondary to disease: cystic fibrosis, cholestatic liver disease, short bowel syndrome, pancreatic insufficiency and bariatric surgery. It also occurs with extremely restricted eating, including the food selectivity seen in some autistic children, where xerophthalmia has been reported.
items.prevalence: WHO estimated that for 1995-2005, 190 million preschool-age children (33.3% of that age group in at-risk populations) and 19.1 million pregnant women had serum retinol below 0.70 micromol/L, with about 5.2 million preschool children affected by night blindness (WHO, Global prevalence of vitamin A deficiency in populations at risk 1995-2005, Geneva 2009). Deficiency in high-income populations is rare and disease-related rather than dietary; no useful population prevalence figure exists for those settings.
items.source: WHO, Global prevalence of vitamin A deficiency in populations at risk 1995-2005, WHO Global Database on Vitamin A Deficiency, Geneva 2009 (ISBN 978 92 4 159801 9); PMID 18806089 (Sommer A, J Nutr 2008, Vitamin A deficiency and clinical disease: an historical overview)
corrections_applied: reversibility: IRREVERSIBLE changed to PARTIAL as instructed by check_report.misclassified. The entry's own note already describes the partial pattern (night blindness and Bitot spots reverse in days to weeks, corneal melt does not), matching how the dataset labels vitamin D, E and K
reversibility_note and all other fields left exactly as written; nothing was softened and the permanence of keratomalacia stands

items.function_short: A plant pigment the body can turn into vitamin A; nothing in the body needs it directly.
items.function_full: Beta-carotene is a provitamin A carotenoid, the orange pigment of carrots, sweet potato, pumpkin and dark green leaves. In the intestinal mucosa, beta-carotene 15,15'-oxygenase (BCO1) cleaves it to retinal, which is reduced to retinol and esterified for storage. The conversion is feedback-regulated and inefficient: the Institute of Medicine assigns 12 micrograms of dietary beta-carotene the vitamin A activity of 1 microgram of retinol. Purified beta-carotene in an oil matrix, the form in a capsule, bypasses the food-matrix release step and carries a separate and much more favourable ratio of 2 micrograms per 1 microgram retinol activity equivalent, so a supplement delivers roughly six times the retinol activity of the same weight eaten in food. Common BCO1 variants reduce conversion markedly in a substantial minority of people. Uncleaved beta-carotene acts as a lipid-phase antioxidant and singlet oxygen quencher in laboratory systems, but no human physiological process depends on the intact molecule, and every requirement it can meet is a vitamin A requirement that preformed retinol meets directly.
items.at_risk: NOT APPLICABLE. Nobody becomes beta-carotene deficient. A diet containing no beta-carotene at all is nutritionally complete provided preformed vitamin A is supplied. For this compound the clinically established direction of effect is harm at supplemental doses rather than any deficiency risk. ATBC is the trial that isolated beta-carotene as a single agent, 20 mg/d in male smokers, raising lung cancer incidence by 18% (95% CI 3-36%) and total mortality by 8% (95% CI 1-16%) (PMID 8127329). CARET tested a combination, 30 mg/d beta-carotene plus 25,000 IU retinol as retinyl palmitate in smokers and asbestos-exposed workers, with lung cancer RR 1.28 (95% CI 1.04-1.57) and all-cause death RR 1.17 (PMID 8602180). The causal attribution to beta-carotene alone therefore rests on ATBC; CARET is supporting evidence for the combination.
items.prevalence: NOT APPLICABLE, since no deficiency state exists. Low plasma carotenoid concentrations are a useful marker of low vegetable intake, not a diagnosis of deficiency, and they carry no defined clinical threshold.
items.source: Institute of Medicine, Dietary Reference Intakes for Vitamin A, Vitamin K, Arsenic, Boron, Chromium, Copper, Iodine, Iron, Manganese, Molybdenum, Nickel, Silicon, Vanadium and Zinc (National Academies Press, 2001), which sets no requirement for beta-carotene and defines both the 12:1 dietary and 2:1 supplemental RAE ratios; PMID 8127329 (ATBC Study Group, N Engl J Med 1994;330:1029-35); PMID 8602180 (Omenn GS et al., CARET, N Engl J Med 1996;334:1150-5); PMID 35727271 (USPSTF Recommendation Statement, JAMA 2022, D recommendation against beta-carotene)
corrections_applied: function_full: added the IOM supplemental ratio (2 micrograms of beta-carotene in oil per 1 microgram RAE) alongside the 12:1 dietary ratio, since quoting only the dietary figure understates a capsule's retinol activity about sixfold

items.function_short: Activates proteins that clot blood and that steer calcium into bone rather than artery walls.
items.function_full: Every form of vitamin K works as the cofactor for gamma-glutamyl carboxylase, the enzyme that converts specific glutamate residues into gamma-carboxyglutamate (Gla), giving those proteins the ability to bind calcium and function. In the liver this activates clotting factors II, VII, IX and X together with the anticoagulant proteins C, S and Z, which is the function the dietary requirement is set on. Outside the liver the same reaction activates osteocalcin in bone and matrix Gla protein in vascular smooth muscle, matrix Gla protein being a local inhibitor of arterial calcification. MK-7 differs from phylloquinone (K1) mainly in pharmacokinetics: a long isoprenoid side chain gives it a circulating half-life of days rather than hours, so it reaches extrahepatic tissue more consistently. MK-4 is the form tissues synthesise for themselves from K1 or menadione via UBIAD1, and as a supplement it clears within hours. Whether raising menaquinone intake above the amount that maintains normal carboxylation changes bone or vascular outcomes is a question about supplementation, separate from the vitamin's essential role.
items.deficiency_name: Vitamin K deficiency bleeding (VKDB), historically called haemorrhagic disease of the newborn. No deficiency disease is attributed to menaquinones specifically: intake recommendations are set for total vitamin K and are based on phylloquinone, and no separate K2 requirement has been established.
items.deficiency_early: A rising PIVKA-II (undercarboxylated prothrombin) is the earliest coagulation marker, followed by a prolonged prothrombin time and raised INR. Clinically, easy bruising, oozing from puncture or venepuncture sites, nosebleeds, bleeding gums or heavy menstrual loss. Undercarboxylated osteocalcin rises before any of the clotting markers, but on its own it is a biochemical finding whose clinical significance is unsettled.
items.deficiency_severe: In newborns, classic VKDB appears in the first week as bleeding from the umbilical stump, gastrointestinal tract, circumcision site or puncture wounds. Late VKDB appears at 2 to 12 weeks and is the dangerous form: roughly half of cases present with intracranial haemorrhage, causing death or lasting neurological injury. In adults with severe malabsorption, cholestasis or prolonged broad-spectrum antibiotics plus poor intake, deficiency produces spontaneous gastrointestinal, retroperitoneal or intracranial bleeding.
items.reversibility_note: The coagulopathy itself corrects completely and quickly: parenteral vitamin K restores clotting factor activity within hours, and prothrombin complex concentrate acts immediately. What does not reverse is the injury from a bleed that has already happened, and intracranial haemorrhage in late VKDB leaves permanent neurological deficit or death in a substantial proportion of affected infants. This is why prophylaxis at birth matters more than treatment.
items.at_risk: Newborns above all, who are born with low stores, receive little vitamin K in breast milk and have an immature gut flora. Intramuscular vitamin K at birth prevents this, and declining or omitting that injection is the main cause of late VKDB in high-income countries today. Beyond infancy: fat malabsorption, cholestasis and biliary obstruction, cystic fibrosis, extensive small bowel resection, and people on vitamin K antagonists such as warfarin, in whom the deficiency is induced on purpose. Dietary vitamin K deficiency in a healthy adult is rare, because phylloquinone is abundant in green vegetables and the liver recycles it efficiently.
items.prevalence: Without prophylaxis, classic VKDB affects an estimated 0.25% to 1.7% of newborns and late VKDB occurs at roughly 4.4 to 7.2 per 100,000 births, the figures used by CDC and the AAP (PMID 24226627). Shearer's surveillance review gives 4 to 7 cases per 100,000 births for Europe and separately reports substantially higher rates from Southeast Asia (PMID 18804903). No population prevalence figure is established for clinical vitamin K deficiency in healthy adults, where it is rare. Undercarboxylated osteocalcin and inactive matrix Gla protein are detectable in a large share of adults, but that is a biomarker observation with no defined clinical deficiency threshold.
items.source: PMID 24226627 (MMWR 2013, Late Vitamin K Deficiency Bleeding in Infants Whose Parents Declined Vitamin K Prophylaxis, Tennessee), source of the 0.25-1.7% classic and 4.4-7.2 per 100,000 late VKDB figures; PMID 18804903 (Shearer MJ, Blood Rev 2009, Vitamin K deficiency bleeding in early infancy), source of the European 4-7 per 100,000 rate and of the higher Southeast Asian rates; doi:10.1146/annurev-nutr-080508-141217 (Booth SL, Annu Rev Nutr 2009;29:89-110, Roles for vitamin K beyond coagulation)

items.function_short: A fish-liver oil supplying vitamin D, preformed vitamin A and omega-3 fats together.
items.function_full: Cod liver oil is a food product, oil rendered from the livers of Gadus species, carrying three active constituents in one dose: vitamin D3, preformed vitamin A as retinyl esters, and the long-chain omega-3 fatty acids EPA and DHA. Each has its own physiology (see the vitamin D3 and preformed vitamin A entries; EPA and DHA are incorporated into membrane phospholipids and serve as precursors to eicosanoids and specialised pro-resolving mediators, with DHA concentrated in retinal photoreceptor and neuronal membranes). It has historical standing because it was the agent that treated and then largely eliminated rickets in the polluted industrial cities of the early twentieth century, before vitamin D itself had been identified. Modern products vary widely in content depending on whether the natural vitamins were stripped during refining and re-added, so the label matters. The practical constraint on dosing is the preformed retinol: an amount large enough to deliver a meaningful EPA and DHA intake can push vitamin A toward or past the tolerable upper limit, and the vitamin A here is retinol, not beta-carotene.
items.deficiency_early: NOT APPLICABLE. Cod liver oil is a product category, not a nutrient. The relevant deficiency states belong to its constituents and are described under the vitamin D3 and preformed vitamin A entries.
items.at_risk: NOT APPLICABLE. No one becomes deficient in cod liver oil. Deficiency risk attaches to its constituent nutrients, principally vitamin D, and is set out in that entry.
items.prevalence: NOT APPLICABLE, product category rather than a nutrient.
items.source: PMID 12897318 (Rajakumar K, Pediatrics 2003;112:e132-5, Vitamin D, cod-liver oil, sunlight, and rickets: a historical perspective)
corrections_applied: No change. The checker flagged nothing in this entry, and NA is the correct state under the NA-versus-NONE rule: cod liver oil is a compound product whose constituent nutrients, vitamin D3 and preformed vitamin A, each have their own entry in this group, so a single deficiency answer would mislead

items.function_short: A mixed low-dose top-up of many nutrients at once; it has no function of its own.
items.function_full: A multivitamin/multimineral is a product category rather than a substance: a fixed combination typically supplying somewhere around the RDA for ten to thirty vitamins and minerals in a single daily dose. It has no physiology of its own, and whatever it does in the body is simply the sum of the individual nutrients, each acting through its own pathway. Formulations differ enormously in which nutrients are included, in what chemical form (iron as sulphate or bisglycinate, folate as folic acid or 5-MTHF, vitamin D as D2 or D3), and at what fraction or multiple of the RDA, so trial evidence about one product transfers poorly to another. Its coherent use is as insurance against gaps in an inadequate diet. A diagnosed deficiency is treated with the specific nutrient at a therapeutic dose, which a multivitamin does not supply.
items.at_risk: NOT APPLICABLE. There is no multivitamin deficiency state. The people for whom a multivitamin is plausibly useful are those with genuinely restricted intake: older adults eating very little total food, people on restrictive or eliminated diets, those with malabsorption, and post-bariatric surgery patients (who need specific high-dose regimens with separate B12, iron and fat-soluble vitamin monitoring rather than a generic multivitamin). In pregnancy the evidence base is for folic acid and iodine specifically, not for the multivitamin as a package.
items.prevalence: NOT APPLICABLE, product category rather than a nutrient. For prevention of cardiovascular disease or cancer in generally healthy, non-pregnant adults the USPSTF concluded in 2022 that evidence is insufficient to judge the balance of benefits and harms (I statement).
items.source: PMID 35727271 (US Preventive Services Task Force Recommendation Statement, JAMA 2022;327(23):2326-2333, Vitamin, Mineral, and Multivitamin Supplementation to Prevent Cardiovascular Disease and Cancer)
corrections_applied: No change. The checker flagged nothing in this entry, and NA is the correct state under the NA-versus-NONE rule: a multivitamin is a compound product whose constituent nutrients each have their own entry, so a single deficiency answer would mislead

items.function_short_zh: 使肠道吸收钙和磷，从而让骨骼正常矿化。
items.function_full_zh: 胆钙化醇在肝脏中被羟化为25-羟维生素D，即血液检测测定的循环储存形式，随后在肾脏中被羟化为1,25-二羟维生素D（骨化三醇），一种通过核内维生素D受体发挥作用的类固醇激素。骨化三醇驱动肠道对钙和磷的主动吸收，抑制甲状旁腺激素，并维持成骨细胞矿化新沉积类骨质所需的钙磷乘积。维生素D受体存在于免疫细胞、肌肉及许多其他组织中，但唯一具有明确人体需求的作用是钙和骨骼轴。皮肤经UVB合成通常提供其中大部分，这也是膳食需求量数据高度取决于纬度、季节和日照的原因。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 生长期儿童表现为佝偻病，成人表现为骨软化症（osteomalacia）。婴儿严重缺乏还可引起低钙血症性惊厥和扩张型心肌病。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 血清25(OH)D首先下降，随后甲状旁腺激素升高（继发性甲状旁腺功能亢进），而血钙仍正常或处于正常低值。此阶段患者几乎无自觉症状：可能有髋部、肋骨和胫骨的隐约酸痛，以及近端肌无力，表现为从矮椅上站起或爬楼梯困难。血液检查显示25(OH)D偏低、PTH升高，且碱性磷酸酶常已升高，此时X线尚无改变。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 儿童期骨骺生长板矿化失败：出现膝内翻或膝外翻、腕踝增宽、肋软骨连接处的佝偻病串珠、行走延迟、生长不良及骨折。婴儿可首先表现为低钙性手足搐搦、惊厥发作或扩张型心肌病，可致命。成人则因未矿化的类骨质堆积而形成骨软化症，出现骨痛、伴摇摆步态的近端肌病，以及Looser带（假性骨折），可进展为耻骨支、股骨颈或肋骨的完全性骨折。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 补充维生素D并配合充足钙摄入后，生化指标、骨痛、肌病、低钙性惊厥及活动性佝偻病的影像学表现通常可完全恢复，一般需数周至数月。但长期佝偻病已形成的骨骼畸形往往持续存在，明显的骨弯曲、佝偻病性侏儒或骨盆畸形可能需要手术矫正。
items.at_risk_zh: 有效日照不足者：居家或机构照护的老年人、全身遮盖皮肤者，以及冬季居于高纬度地区者。高纬度地区深肤色人群（黑色素较多意味着UVB合成较少）。未额外补充维生素D的纯母乳喂养婴儿，因母乳中维生素D含量低。肥胖者（脂肪组织中维生素D被隔离）。乳糜泻、囊性纤维化、胆汁淤积或减重手术导致的脂肪吸收不良者。慢性肾病或肝病患者，以及长期使用抗惊厥药或糖皮质激素者。
items.prevalence_zh: NHANES 2011-2014年数据：美国1岁及以上人群中，5.0%血清25(OH)D低于30 nmol/L（属缺乏风险），18.3%处于30至49.9 nmol/L之间；低于30 nmol/L的比例在非西班牙裔黑人中为17.5%，而非西班牙裔白人中仅为2.1%（PMID 31076739）。临床营养性佝偻病在高收入国家已不常见但并未消失，在中东、非洲及南亚部分地区仍较为常见（PMID 26741135）。

items.supplement: Vitamin E at or above 400 IU/d
items.function_short_zh: 人体主要的脂溶性抗氧化剂，保护细胞膜和神经免受氧化损伤。
items.function_full_zh: α-生育酚是人体唯一保留的维生素E形式。吸收后，肝脏中的α-生育酚转运蛋白（TTPA）选择性地将α-生育酚装载到VLDL上以输送至各组织，而其余的生育酚及生育三烯酚则被代谢并排出。其确立的功能是阻断细胞膜及脂蛋白中多不饱和脂肪酸的脂质过氧化链式反应，向脂质过氧自由基提供一个氢原子，随后由抗坏血酸再生。缺乏时最先受损的组织是周围神经轴突、脊髓后索和小脑、视网膜以及红细胞膜。按正确换算（1 mg α-生育酚=1.49 IU天然来源RRR型，或2.22 IU合成all-rac型），400 IU相当于268 mg天然来源或180 mg合成α-生育酚，约为成人RDA（15 mg/d）的12至18倍，具体倍数取决于产品所用的形式，因此该剂量已是药理性使用，超出了纠正膳食摄入不足所需的范围。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 没有单一命名的经典疾病。公认的综合征是维生素E缺乏性共济失调，一种伴周围神经病变和色素性视网膜病变的脊髓小脑变性；早产儿则表现为早产儿溶血性贫血。孤立性维生素E缺乏性共济失调（AVED）临床表现相同，但其病因是遗传性TTPA基因缺陷，并非由膳食缺乏引起。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 血浆α-生育酚低于约12 micromol/L，或生育酚与总脂质比值偏低，通常先于症状出现数月至数年，是实用的监测指标。最早的临床体征是踝反射消失，以及足部振动觉和关节位置觉减退，有时伴暗处行走不稳。早产儿则表现为溶血性贫血伴网织红细胞升高。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 若不治疗，将进展为脊髓小脑及感觉联合受损的表现：后索变性所致共济失调、构音障碍、眼肌麻痹、头部震颤、近端肌无力，以及伴视力下降的色素性视网膜病变。终末阶段患者无法独立行走，遗留固定性感觉性共济失调和神经病变。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 大剂量补充能可靠地阻止病情进展，若在早期开始治疗（症状出现后约一年内，或在已知吸收不良的患儿出现症状之前），大部分神经病变可恢复。长期存在的脊髓后索和小脑变性以及已形成的视网膜病变通常无法完全恢复，因此治疗的作用重在预防，已造成的损害难以逆转。
items.at_risk_zh: 几乎仅见于脂肪吸收障碍者：囊性纤维化、胆汁淤积性肝病及胆道闭锁、短肠综合征、慢性胰腺炎、无β脂蛋白血症及纯合子低β脂蛋白血症。早产儿及极低出生体重儿。另外还有遗传性TTPA缺陷（AVED）患者，这是一种遗传性转运障碍，与膳食无关。脂肪吸收正常的成人，即使维生素E摄入过少，基本上也不会产生临床缺乏。就本条目所指400 IU/d剂量而言，已确立的效应方向是危害，并非补充效果：在SELECT试验中，400 IU/d α-生育酚使健康男性前列腺癌发生率升高（HR 1.17，99% CI 1.004-1.36；PMID 21990298）。
items.prevalence_zh: 明显临床缺乏无确切数据，在普通人群中足够罕见，因此没有有意义的患病率数据。广为引用的说法称超过90%美国人的α-生育酚摄入未达到平均需要量估计值，这只是摄入量统计，不是缺乏率，也没有相应的神经系统疾病负担伴随（doi:10.3945/an.114.006254）。未经治疗的囊性纤维化和胆汁淤积性肝病患者中，生化性缺乏较为常见。

items.supplement: Preformed vitamin A at or above 10,000 IU
items.supplement_zh: 预成型维生素A（10,000 IU及以上）
items.function_short_zh: 生成眼睛暗光视觉所需的色素，并维持皮肤、肠道及呼吸道黏膜的健康。
items.function_full_zh: 视黄醇被氧化为11-顺式视黄醛，后者与视蛋白结合形成视紫红质，即视杆细胞的感光色素，使暗光视觉成为可能。经另一条途径，它被氧化为全反式及9-顺式视黄酸，是核内RAR和RXR受体的配体，调控相关基因的转录，这些基因控制上皮分化（结膜、角膜、呼吸道及肠道中杯状细胞和黏蛋白生成）、胚胎发育模式形成、造血功能，以及包括T淋巴细胞归巢肠道在内的固有免疫和适应性免疫。来自肝脏、乳制品、蛋类及补充剂的预成型视黄醇吸收效率高，储存于肝星状细胞中，可缓冲血浆浓度长达数月。10,000 IU约为3,000 micrograms视黄醇活性当量，约为成人RDA的四倍，已达到可耐受最高摄入量水平。因此在此剂量下，临床上真正需要关注的是过量问题，摄入不足并非重点。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 眼干燥症（xerophthalmia），谱系涵盖从夜盲症（nyctalopia）到结膜及角膜干燥，再到角膜软化症（keratomalacia）。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 首先出现暗适应障碍，随后是明显的夜盲：黄昏后或光线昏暗房间中视物困难，幼儿则表现为天黑后不愿活动。随后出现结膜干燥及Bitot斑（结膜角化形成的泡沫状灰白三角形斑块）。麻疹、腹泻及呼吸道感染的加重和病程延长常先于任何眼部体征出现。血清视黄醇低于0.70 micromol/L是生化指标，但只有在肝脏储备大量耗竭后才会下降。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 角膜干燥进展为点状角膜病变，继而角膜溃疡，最终发展为角膜软化症：角膜基质在数天内液化，常伴穿孔。眼球结构被破坏，失明为永久性。缺乏还会大幅提高儿童因麻疹、腹泻及呼吸道感染导致的死亡率，因此致盲的儿童中约半数在12个月内死亡。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 大剂量视黄醇治疗后，夜盲、结膜干燥及Bitot斑可在数天至数周内恢复。一旦角膜发生溃疡或液化，损害即为结构性且永久性的，维生素A缺乏症至今仍是全球儿童可预防性失明的主要病因之一。在病情严重、储备耗竭的患儿中，从完全可逆到不可逆阶段之间的窗口期可能仅有数天，这也是临床一旦怀疑即予治疗、不等视黄醇检测结果的原因。
items.at_risk_zh: 低收入地区膳食中动物性食物或维生素A原蔬菜摄入不足的学龄前儿童及孕产妇，尤其在麻疹和腹泻性疾病常见的地区。在高收入国家，缺乏症罕见，几乎总是继发于疾病：囊性纤维化、胆汁淤积性肝病、短肠综合征、胰腺功能不全及减重手术。极度受限的饮食也可导致缺乏，包括部分自闭症儿童表现出的食物选择性，其中已有眼干燥症的病例报告。
items.prevalence_zh: 世界卫生组织估计，1995至2005年间，190 million名学龄前儿童（占高危人群该年龄段的33.3%）及19.1 million名孕妇血清视黄醇低于0.70 micromol/L，其中约5.2 million名学龄前儿童患有夜盲症（WHO, Global prevalence of vitamin A deficiency in populations at risk 1995-2005, Geneva 2009）。高收入人群中的缺乏症罕见，多与疾病相关，与膳食因素关系不大；这些地区尚无有意义的人群患病率数据。

items.function_short_zh: 一种植物色素，人体可将其转化为维生素A；人体没有任何过程直接需要它本身。
items.function_full_zh: β-胡萝卜素是一种维生素A原类胡萝卜素，是胡萝卜、红薯、南瓜及深绿色叶菜中的橙色色素。在肠黏膜中，β-胡萝卜素15,15'-加氧酶（beta-carotene 15,15'-oxygenase, BCO1）将其裂解为视黄醛，后者被还原为视黄醇并酯化储存。这一转化受反馈调节且效率不高：美国医学研究所（Institute of Medicine）将12 micrograms膳食β-胡萝卜素的维生素A活性定为等同于1 microgram视黄醇。以油基质形式存在的纯化β-胡萝卜素，即胶囊中的形式，绕过了食物基质的释放步骤，其换算比例更有利，为2 micrograms对应1 microgram视黄醇活性当量，因此补充剂提供的视黄醇活性约为同等重量食物摄入的六倍。常见的BCO1基因变异会使相当一部分人群的转化效率显著降低。未被裂解的β-胡萝卜素在实验体系中可作为脂相抗氧化剂及单线态氧猝灭剂，但人体没有任何生理过程依赖完整分子本身，而它所能满足的一切需求，都是预成型视黄醇可以直接满足的维生素A需求。
items.at_risk_zh: 不适用。没有人会发生β-胡萝卜素缺乏。只要提供了预成型维生素A，完全不含β-胡萝卜素的膳食在营养上也是完整的。就该化合物而言，临床已确立的效应方向是补充剂量下的危害，缺乏风险则没有实际证据支持。ATBC是将β-胡萝卜素作为单一制剂分离出来检验的试验，男性吸烟者每日20 mg，使肺癌发生率升高18%（95% CI 3-36%），总死亡率升高8%（95% CI 1-16%）（PMID 8127329）。CARET试验测试的是联合方案，吸烟者及石棉暴露工人每日服用30 mg β-胡萝卜素加25,000 IU视黄醇棕榈酸酯，肺癌RR为1.28（95% CI 1.04-1.57），全因死亡RR为1.17（PMID 8602180）。因此，将因果关系归于β-胡萝卜素单一因素的证据来自ATBC；CARET则为联合方案提供了支持性证据。
items.prevalence_zh: 不适用，因为不存在缺乏状态。血浆类胡萝卜素浓度低是蔬菜摄入不足的有用指标，不是缺乏症的诊断依据，也没有明确的临床阈值。

items.function_short_zh: 激活促使血液凝固的蛋白，以及引导钙沉积于骨骼而非动脉壁的蛋白。
items.function_full_zh: 各种形式的维生素K都作为γ-谷氨酰羧化酶（gamma-glutamyl carboxylase）的辅因子发挥作用，该酶将特定谷氨酸残基转化为γ-羧基谷氨酸（Gla），使相关蛋白获得结合钙并发挥功能的能力。在肝脏中，这一反应激活凝血因子II、VII、IX和X，以及抗凝蛋白C、S和Z，这也是膳食需求量所依据的功能。在肝脏之外，同样的反应激活骨骼中的骨钙素（osteocalcin）及血管平滑肌中的基质Gla蛋白（matrix Gla protein），后者是动脉钙化的局部抑制因子。MK-7与叶绿醌（phylloquinone，K1）的主要区别在于药代动力学：其较长的异戊二烯侧链使其循环半衰期为数天而非数小时，因而能更稳定地到达肝外组织。MK-4是组织通过UBIAD1由K1或甲萘醌自行合成的形式，作为补充剂时其清除时间为数小时。将甲萘醌摄入量提高到超过维持正常羧化所需水平是否会改变骨骼或血管相关结局，属于补充剂层面的问题，不同于该维生素本身的必需作用。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 维生素K缺乏性出血（vitamin K deficiency bleeding, VKDB），历史上称为新生儿出血病。没有专门归因于甲萘醌类（menaquinones）的缺乏性疾病：摄入推荐量是针对总维生素K制定的，且以叶绿醌为基础，尚未确立单独的K2需求量。
items.deficiency_early_zh: PIVKA-II（羧化不足的凝血酶原）升高是最早的凝血指标，随后出现凝血酶原时间延长及INR升高。临床上表现为易出现瘀斑、穿刺或静脉穿刺部位渗血、鼻出血、牙龈出血或月经过多。羧化不足的骨钙素升高早于任何凝血指标，但其单独出现只是一项生化发现，临床意义尚无定论。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 新生儿中，经典型VKDB在出生第一周内出现，表现为脐残端、消化道、包皮环切部位或穿刺伤口出血。迟发型VKDB出现于出生后2至12周，是危险性更高的类型：约半数病例表现为颅内出血，导致死亡或永久性神经损伤。成人中，若存在严重吸收不良、胆汁淤积，或长期使用广谱抗生素合并摄入不足，缺乏可导致自发性消化道、腹膜后或颅内出血。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 凝血功能障碍本身可完全且迅速纠正：肠外途径给予维生素K可在数小时内恢复凝血因子活性，凝血酶原复合物浓缩剂则可立即起效。无法逆转的是已经发生的出血所造成的损伤，迟发型VKDB中的颅内出血会使相当一部分患儿遗留永久性神经损害或死亡。这正是出生时预防性用药比事后治疗更重要的原因。
items.at_risk_zh: 首要的高危人群是新生儿，出生时储备低，母乳中维生素K含量少，肠道菌群尚未成熟。出生时肌注维生素K可预防这一情况，如今在高收入国家，迟发型VKDB的主要原因正是拒绝或漏打这一针剂。婴儿期之外的高危人群包括：脂肪吸收不良、胆汁淤积及胆道梗阻、囊性纤维化、广泛小肠切除，以及服用华法林等维生素K拮抗剂者（这类患者的缺乏是有意诱导产生的）。健康成人的膳食性维生素K缺乏罕见，因为叶绿醌广泛存在于绿叶蔬菜中，且肝脏能高效地将其循环利用。
items.prevalence_zh: 在未预防的情况下，经典型VKDB估计影响0.25%至1.7%的新生儿，迟发型VKDB发生率约为每100,000活产4.4至7.2例，这是CDC和AAP采用的数据（PMID 24226627）。Shearer的监测综述给出欧洲每100,000活产4至7例的数据，并另外报告东南亚地区的发生率明显更高（PMID 18804903）。健康成人临床维生素K缺乏症尚无确立的人群患病率数据，该情况在成人中较为罕见。羧化不足的骨钙素及无活性的基质Gla蛋白在很大一部分成人中均可检出，但这只是一项生物标志物观察结果，没有明确的临床缺乏阈值。

items.function_short_zh: 一种鱼肝来源的油，同时提供维生素D、预成型维生素A及omega-3脂肪。
items.function_full_zh: 鱼肝油是一种食品，由鳕属（Gadus）鱼类的肝脏炼制而成，一次服用即含三种活性成分：维生素D3、以视黄酯形式存在的预成型维生素A，以及长链omega-3脂肪酸EPA和DHA。三者各有其自身的生理作用（参见维生素D3及预成型维生素A条目；EPA和DHA被纳入膜磷脂，并作为类花生酸及特化促消退介质的前体，其中DHA集中于视网膜光感受器和神经元膜中）。鱼肝油具有历史地位，因为在维生素D本身被鉴定出来之前，它正是在20世纪初污染严重的工业城市中用于治疗并进而大幅消除佝偻病的制剂。现代产品含量差异很大，取决于精炼过程中是否去除了天然维生素并重新添加，因此标签内容很重要。剂量的实际限制因素是其中的预成型视黄醇：足以提供有意义EPA和DHA摄入量的剂量，可能使维生素A摄入逼近或超过可耐受最高摄入量，且这里的维生素A是视黄醇，不是β-胡萝卜素。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 不适用。鱼肝油是一个产品类别，而非营养素本身。相关的缺乏状态属于其各组成成分，已在维生素D3及预成型维生素A条目中说明。
items.at_risk_zh: 不适用。没有人会发生鱼肝油缺乏。缺乏风险属于其组成营养素，主要是维生素D，已在该条目中说明。
items.prevalence_zh: 不适用，属于产品类别而非营养素。

items.supplement_zh: 复合维生素/复合矿物质
items.function_short_zh: 多种营养素的低剂量混合补充；它本身没有独立的功能。
items.function_full_zh: 复合维生素/复合矿物质是一个产品类别，而非单一物质：通常是一种固定组合，每日一剂提供约十至三十种维生素和矿物质，剂量大致接近其RDA。它本身没有独立的生理作用，其在体内产生的任何效果，都只是各单独营养素作用的总和，每种营养素通过各自的途径发挥作用。不同配方在所含营养素种类、化学形式（铁为硫酸盐还是双甘氨酸螯合物，叶酸为folic acid还是5-MTHF，维生素D为D2还是D3）以及占RDA的比例或倍数上差异极大，因此针对某一产品的试验证据很难推及另一产品。其合理用途是作为膳食摄入不足的保险性补充。已确诊的缺乏症需以特定营养素的治疗剂量进行纠正，复合维生素无法提供这样的剂量。
items.at_risk_zh: 不适用。不存在复合维生素缺乏状态。可能从复合维生素中获益的人群，是那些确实摄入受限的人：总体进食量很少的老年人、饮食受限或有饮食排除的人、吸收不良患者，以及减重手术后患者（这类患者需要特定的高剂量方案，并单独监测B12、铁及脂溶性维生素，不能仅靠通用复合维生素）。在妊娠期，证据基础具体支持的是叶酸和碘。复合维生素作为整体组合并无相应证据基础。
items.prevalence_zh: 不适用，属于产品类别而非营养素。对于总体健康、非孕期成人预防心血管疾病或癌症，USPSTF在2022年得出结论，认为现有证据不足以判断利弊平衡（I级声明）。

items.function_short: Supplies the one-carbon units cells need to build DNA and divide.
items.function_full: Folate is reduced to tetrahydrofolate, which carries one-carbon groups for thymidylate and purine synthesis and for the remethylation of homocysteine to methionine by methionine synthase (a B12-dependent enzyme). Tissues that divide fastest depend on it most: bone marrow, gut mucosa, and the closing neural tube of an early embryo. Folic acid is the synthetic, fully oxidised form; it must be reduced by dihydrofolate reductase, whose capacity in humans is limited, so unmetabolised folic acid appears in plasma at intakes above roughly 200 to 400 micrograms in one dose. The natural circulating form is 5-methyltetrahydrofolate.
items.deficiency_name: Megaloblastic (macrocytic) anaemia. In early pregnancy, low folate status raises the risk of neural tube defects (anencephaly, spina bifida, encephalocele); periconceptional folic acid prevents a large proportion but not all of them.
items.deficiency_early: Serum folate falls first, then red cell folate. Raised mean corpuscular volume appears before anaemia, with hypersegmented neutrophils on the film. Symptoms are non-specific: tiredness, breathlessness on exertion, sore tongue, mouth ulcers, mild diarrhoea. In pregnancy there are no maternal warning signs at all; the first evidence of a neural tube defect is usually the anomaly scan.
items.deficiency_severe: Marrow failure with pancytopenia, severe anaemia, mucosal ulceration and malabsorptive diarrhoea. In pregnancy the severe endpoint is structural: anencephaly is incompatible with life, and open spina bifida causes lifelong paralysis below the lesion, hydrocephalus, and bowel and bladder impairment.
items.reversibility_note: The haematological and mucosal effects reverse completely: reticulocytosis begins within a week and the blood count normalises in about two months, with no residual deficit. A neural tube defect that has already formed is permanent and cannot be reversed by any later intake. The neural tube closes 26 to 28 days after conception, so supplementation started after a positive pregnancy test is too late for that specific endpoint, which is the whole argument for taking it before conception.
items.at_risk: Women who could become pregnant, particularly with an unplanned pregnancy. Coeliac disease and other malabsorption. Heavy alcohol use. Drugs that block folate handling: methotrexate, sulfasalazine, trimethoprim, phenytoin and other anticonvulsants. High-turnover states such as chronic haemolysis and exfoliative skin disease. Dialysis.
items.prevalence: In the fortified United States, 18.6% of women aged 12 to 49 had red cell folate below the threshold associated with elevated neural tube defect risk (748 nmol/L) in 2011 to 2016, down from 23.2% in 2007 to 2010 (PMID 31504109). Frank folate-deficiency anaemia is now uncommon where fortification is mandatory and is seen more often where it is not.
items.source: PMID 31504109 (Pfeiffer et al., Am J Clin Nutr 2019, US folate status 20 years after fortification); PMID 1677062 (MRC Vitamin Study, Lancet 1991: 4 mg/day periconceptional folic acid cut neural tube defect recurrence by 72%, RR 0.28, 95% CI 0.12 to 0.71)
corrections_applied: deficiency_name: replaced the deterministic claim that folate deficiency causes neural tube defects with the probabilistic form supplied by the checker (low folate status raises NTD risk; periconceptional folic acid prevents a large proportion but not all of them). Risk stays risk, and the size of the prevention effect is not softened.

prevalence: the unsourced claim that folate-deficiency anaemia 'remains common' in unfortified settings was softened to 'is seen more often where it is not', because PMID 31504109 is a fortified-US survey and contains no unfortified-country comparison. The fortified-US figures and the 748 nmol/L cutoff were verified by the checker and kept verbatim.

items.function_short: Needed by two enzymes: one for making new blood cells, one for nerve insulation.
items.function_full: Cobalamin is the cofactor for exactly two human enzymes. Methionine synthase remethylates homocysteine to methionine using 5-methyltetrahydrofolate, which both regenerates usable folate and supplies S-adenosylmethionine for the methylation reactions that maintain myelin. Methylmalonyl-CoA mutase converts methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA in the mitochondrion during breakdown of odd-chain fatty acids and branched-chain amino acids. Absorption is elaborate: gastric acid and pepsin release B12 from food protein, intrinsic factor from parietal cells carries it, and receptors in the terminal ileum take it up. Outside vegan diets the usual cause of deficiency is failure somewhere along that route rather than low intake.
items.deficiency_name: Pernicious anaemia (autoimmune intrinsic factor failure) and subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord; megaloblastic anaemia is the haematological presentation.
items.deficiency_early: Methylmalonic acid and homocysteine rise before serum B12 drops into the clearly deficient range, which is why borderline results are often followed with those metabolites. Symmetrical tingling and numbness in the feet and hands, loss of vibration sense and joint position sense, unsteadiness that is worse in the dark. Macrocytosis with hypersegmented neutrophils, sore smooth tongue, fatigue, mild cognitive slowing and low mood. Neurological signs can be present with a completely normal full blood count.
items.deficiency_severe: Subacute combined degeneration: demyelination of the dorsal columns and lateral corticospinal tracts producing sensory ataxia, spasticity, extensor plantar responses, and bladder and bowel disturbance, progressing untreated to spastic paraparesis and loss of independent walking. Optic atrophy occurs in a minority, as do dementia and psychosis. Severe megaloblastic anaemia with pancytopenia can occur, but it is the neurology that disables.
items.reversibility_note: The blood corrects fully (reticulocytosis within a week, counts normal in roughly eight weeks) while the neurology may not. In the largest series, 153 episodes in 143 patients, 47.1% had complete resolution of neurological abnormalities on treatment and 6.3% were left with moderate-to-severe residual disability; so most treated patients recover fully or nearly so and a minority are left disabled. What survives treatment is inversely related to how severe the deficits were and how long they had run before treatment started. Recovery is fastest in the first two months and continues to about six months. This is exactly why folate must not be given blind for an unexplained macrocytic anaemia: folic acid repairs the blood picture and removes the visible signal while the cord damage carries on.
items.at_risk: Adults over 60 with atrophic gastritis and food-bound B12 malabsorption. Autoimmune pernicious anaemia. Gastrectomy or gastric bypass, ileal resection, Crohn's disease. Long-term metformin. Long-term proton pump inhibitors or H2 blockers. Strict vegans and, importantly, their exclusively breastfed infants. Repeated nitrous oxide exposure, recreational or occupational, which inactivates methionine synthase directly.
items.prevalence: About 6% of people aged 60 and over in large US and UK surveys have plasma B12 below 148 pmol/L, and close to 20% are in the marginal range of 148 to 221 pmol/L; prevalence rises with age and is considerably higher in low-income countries across the whole life span (PMID 19116323).
items.source: PMID 19116323 (Allen, Am J Clin Nutr 2009, How common is vitamin B-12 deficiency?); PMID 1648656 (Healton et al., Medicine 1991, 153 episodes of neurological cobalamin deficiency; residual deficit predicted by severity and duration before treatment)
corrections_applied: reversibility_note: removed 'deficits present for six to twelve months or more often leave permanent...', which ran ahead of the cited paper, and replaced it with Healton 1991's actual figures (47.1% complete resolution, 6.3% moderate-to-severe residual disability) plus the finding the paper does establish, that residual deficit scales inversely with pre-treatment severity and duration.
reversibility: kept IRREVERSIBLE, as the checker directed. The permanence is real for the minority left with cord damage, so the classification was not downgraded along with the wording.

items.function_short: Vitamin B6 powers amino acid enzymes; at high doses it damages sensory nerves.
items.function_full: The active form, pyridoxal 5'-phosphate, is the cofactor for well over 100 enzymes, most of them in amino acid metabolism: transaminases, the decarboxylases that make serotonin, dopamine, GABA and histamine, the first committed step of haem synthesis (ALA synthase), glycogen phosphorylase, and cystathionine beta-synthase and gamma-lyase, which dispose of homocysteine by transsulphuration. Requirement rises with protein intake. Above the point where these enzymes are saturated, extra B6 adds no function. High-dose products (typically 50 to 500 mg/day, sold for premenstrual symptoms, carpal tunnel syndrome, nausea in pregnancy, or hidden inside B-complex and energy formulations) instead produce a dose-dependent and duration-dependent sensory neuropathy, with the dorsal root ganglion as the target. On toxicity, which is a separate question from the deficiency rated below: because the injury is to the sensory nerve cell bodies in the dorsal root ganglion rather than to the axon alone, recovery after stopping the supplement is often incomplete. Numbness and impaired position sense usually improve over several months, sometimes substantially, but residual deficit persists in some people (Schaumburg 1983). Time to onset is inversely related to dose, so grams per day can do it in weeks while tens of milligrams may take years, which is why EFSA applied an uncertainty factor of 4 to a 50 mg/day reference point when setting the 12 mg/day adult upper level in 2023.
items.deficiency_name: Pyridoxine deficiency: seborrhoeic dermatitis with cheilosis and glossitis, hypochromic microcytic anaemia, and seizures in infants; nearly always secondary to isoniazid, cycloserine, hydralazine or penicillamine, alcohol dependence, dialysis or malabsorption.
items.deficiency_early: Plasma pyridoxal 5'-phosphate below about 20 nmol/L, usually with no symptoms at all. When symptoms appear they are mucocutaneous and non-specific: angular cheilitis, glossitis, seborrhoeic dermatitis around the eyes, nose and mouth, plus irritability and low mood. Homocysteine may be mildly raised.
items.deficiency_severe: Hypochromic microcytic anaemia from impaired haem synthesis (distinct from X-linked ALAS2 pyridoxine-responsive sideroblastic anaemia, which is genetic, not dietary), and a peripheral sensory neuropathy. In infants, deficiency causes seizures through failure of GABA synthesis. Isolated severe deficiency is rare and is nearly always secondary: isoniazid, cycloserine, hydralazine or penicillamine treatment, alcohol dependence, dialysis, or malabsorption. Note that both deficiency and excess of B6 produce peripheral neuropathy, so neuropathy in a supplement user is at least as likely to be caused by the supplement as corrected by it.
items.reversibility_note: This field rates recovery from the deficiency, and B6 deficiency corrects fully within weeks on modest repletion, with no residual deficit: the mucocutaneous signs clear, the anaemia resolves, and pyridoxine-responsive infantile seizures stop once the vitamin is given. Recovery from high-dose B6 neuropathy is a different question with a different answer (often incomplete) and is set out in the function description above, not here.
items.at_risk: For deficiency: people taking isoniazid, cycloserine, hydralazine or penicillamine; alcohol dependence; dialysis; malabsorption. Lower plasma PLP is also seen in older adults, smokers, and current or former oral contraceptive users. For toxicity: anyone taking a high-dose B6 or B-complex product for months to years, often without realising the dose, since a single tablet can exceed the European upper level several-fold.
items.prevalence: Around 23 to 27% of US adults not taking supplements had plasma PLP below 20 nmol/L in NHANES 2003 to 2004, mostly biochemical rather than symptomatic (PMID 18469270). On the toxicity side, EFSA set the adult tolerable upper intake at 12 mg/day in 2023, derived from a 50 mg/day reference point for peripheral neuropathy with an uncertainty factor of 4 (doi:10.2903/j.efsa.2023.8006).
items.source: PMID 18469270 (Morris et al., Am J Clin Nutr 2008, plasma PLP in NHANES 2003 to 2004); PMID 6308447 (Schaumburg et al., N Engl J Med 1983, sensory neuropathy from pyridoxine abuse); doi:10.2903/j.efsa.2023.8006 (EFSA 2023, tolerable upper intake level for vitamin B6)
corrections_applied: deficiency_state: FUNCTIONAL changed to CLINICAL per the misclassified list. FUNCTIONAL paired with deficiency_name NONE was self-contradictory and contradicted the row's own text, which describes a named clinical syndrome.

deficiency_name: NONE replaced with the named syndrome, as a CLINICAL row must name the disease. Used the checker's wording (dermatitis with cheilosis and glossitis, hypochromic microcytic anaemia, infantile seizures; nearly always secondary).

reversibility: PARTIAL changed to FULL per the misclassified list. PARTIAL was rating recovery from B6 excess, the only row in the group where the column silently meant toxicity instead of deficiency, and the row's own note conceded the deficiency corrects fully.

reversibility_note: rewritten to describe deficiency recovery only. The dorsal root ganglion mechanism, incomplete recovery from high-dose neuropathy, and the dose-inverse time to onset were moved verbatim in substance into function_full rather than dropped, since the clinical content is accurate.

deficiency_severe: 'microcytic sideroblastic anaemia' replaced with 'hypochromic microcytic anaemia from impaired haem synthesis (distinct from X-linked ALAS2 pyridoxine-responsive sideroblastic anaemia, which is genetic, not dietary)', keeping the genetic disorder out of the dietary-deficiency slot.

items.function_short: Keeps collagen strong and wounds healing; without it blood vessels and gums break down.
items.function_full: Ascorbate is the reducing cofactor that keeps the iron atom in a family of dioxygenases in its active state. The best known are prolyl-4-hydroxylase and lysyl hydroxylase, which hydroxylate collagen so the triple helix is stable and can be cross-linked; without them the collagen laid down is defective, which explains bleeding, poor wound healing and the reopening of old scars. The same chemistry serves dopamine beta-hydroxylase (noradrenaline synthesis), peptidylglycine alpha-amidating monooxygenase (peptide hormone amidation), two carnitine biosynthesis enzymes, and the HIF prolyl hydroxylases and TET and JmjC demethylases in gene regulation. Ascorbate also reduces dietary non-haem iron to the absorbable ferrous form. Humans cannot synthesise it because the gulonolactone oxidase gene is inactive.
items.deficiency_early: After roughly one to three months of intake below about 10 mg/day, plasma ascorbate falls and body stores drop under about 300 mg. The first phase is fatigue, irritability and diffuse aching in the legs, with nothing visible. Then come the specific skin signs: perifollicular hyperkeratosis with corkscrew-shaped body hairs on the thighs and shins, perifollicular haemorrhage, easy bruising, and swollen, spongy, bleeding gums in anyone who still has teeth.
items.deficiency_severe: Bleeding into skin, muscle and joints, haemarthrosis, and subperiosteal haemorrhage, which in children causes severe limb pain and refusal to move (pseudoparalysis). Old wounds and scars break down, teeth loosen and are lost, anaemia and oedema develop. Untreated scurvy is fatal, usually from haemorrhage or cardiac failure, though it very rarely reaches that stage in current practice because treatment is trivially available.
items.reversibility_note: Complete and unusually fast. Fatigue and pain begin improving within 24 to 48 hours of treatment, bleeding gums and bruising settle over one to two weeks, and full recovery takes around three months on 100 to 300 mg/day. No permanent deficit remains. The only exception is teeth already lost, which do not grow back.
items.at_risk: People whose diets contain almost no fruit or vegetables: highly restrictive or selective eaters including some autistic children, people living alone with severe mental illness or dementia, alcohol and drug dependence, homelessness and food insecurity. Also smokers (requirement about 35 mg/day higher), people on dialysis, malabsorption, and some patients after bariatric surgery. Scurvy is a disease of dietary pattern, not of insufficient supplementation; roughly 10 mg/day prevents it and a single orange comfortably exceeds that.
items.prevalence: 7.1% (SE 0.9) of the US population aged 6 and over had serum ascorbate below 11.4 micromol/L in NHANES 2003 to 2004, down from about 13% in NHANES III, with the highest rates in smokers and low-income groups (PMID 19675106).
items.source: PMID 19675106 (Schleicher et al., Am J Clin Nutr 2009, serum vitamin C and prevalence of deficiency in the United States, NHANES 2003 to 2004)
corrections_applied: No errors and no misclassifications were flagged against this entry; the checker verified its figures (7.1% SE 0.9, down from about 13% in NHANES III) and its FULL reversibility rating. Retained unchanged.

items.supplement: High-dose folic acid plus B12 for cardiovascular prevention
items.function_short: Lowers homocysteine in the blood, which turns out not to prevent heart attacks.
items.function_full: Folic acid with B12, often with B6 added, reliably lowers plasma total homocysteine by roughly a quarter, because both vitamins feed the methionine synthase step that converts homocysteine back to methionine. The rationale was observational: raised homocysteine tracks with vascular disease and stroke. Randomised trials separated the biomarker from the disease. The Cochrane review included 15 trials and 71,422 participants in total, with each outcome pooled from a subset of those trials: no effect on myocardial infarction (7.1% versus 6.0%, RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.95 to 1.10; 12 trials, 46,699 participants) and none on death from any cause (11.7% versus 12.3%, RR 1.01, 95% CI 0.96 to 1.06; 11 trials, 44,817 participants), with a small reduction in stroke (4.3% versus 5.1%, RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.82 to 0.99; 10 trials, 44,224 participants) driven largely by trials in populations without folic acid fortification and with low baseline folate. One safety point carries over from the components: high-dose folic acid given without first checking B12 status can normalise the anaemia of B12 deficiency while the spinal cord damage continues undetected, so B12 status should be established before folate is given at these doses.
items.deficiency_early: NOT APPLICABLE. This is a therapeutic regimen tested for cardiovascular prevention, not a nutrient. The deficiency states of the two components are covered in their own entries.
items.deficiency_severe: NOT APPLICABLE. There is no deficiency of a combination product.
items.reversibility_note: NOT APPLICABLE. No deficiency state exists for an intervention category.
items.at_risk: NOT APPLICABLE. No deficiency state exists for an intervention category.
items.prevalence: NOT APPLICABLE. For scale of effect rather than deficiency: Cochrane derives a number needed to treat for benefit of 143 (95% CI 85 to 428) over 5.4 years to prevent one stroke, and that figure comes from the folic acid plus enalapril comparison (the CSPPT trial in an unfortified Chinese hypertensive population), not from the pooled 10-trial stroke estimate (PMID 28816346).
items.source: PMID 28816346 (Marti-Carvajal et al., Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2017, homocysteine-lowering interventions for preventing cardiovascular events, 15 trials, 71,422 participants)
corrections_applied: function_full: the whole-review denominator (15 trials, 71,422 participants) was attached to every outcome estimate. Restored the per-outcome denominators verbatim from the correction: MI 12 trials / 46,699, all-cause death 11 trials / 44,817, stroke 10 trials / 44,224, with 15 trials / 71,422 kept as the review total. All effect estimates and percentages were verified correct and left untouched.
function_full: added the all-cause-death event percentages (11.7% versus 12.3%), which had been dropped while MI and stroke kept theirs.

prevalence: the NNTB of 143 now carries its confidence interval (95% CI 85 to 428) and names the comparison it belongs to (folic acid plus enalapril, the CSPPT trial in an unfortified population), replacing the vague hedge 'in the trial setting where the stroke signal appeared'.

deficiency_state NA retained: this is a compound regimen whose two constituents each have their own entry in this group, which is the one case where NA rather than NONE is correct. All deficiency fields remain NOT APPLICABLE and reversibility remains NA.

items.function_short_zh: 提供细胞合成DNA和分裂所需的一碳单位。
items.function_full_zh: 叶酸被还原为四氢叶酸，携带一碳基团用于胸苷酸和嘌呤合成，也用于同型半胱氨酸在methionine synthase（一种依赖B12的酶）催化下再甲基化生成蛋氨酸。分裂最快的组织对它依赖程度最高：骨髓、肠黏膜，以及早期胚胎正在闭合的神经管。叶酸是人工合成的完全氧化形式，必须经dihydrofolate reductase还原，该酶在人体内的能力有限，因此单次摄入量超过约200至400微克时，血浆中就会出现未代谢的叶酸。天然的循环形式是5-甲基四氢叶酸。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 巨幼细胞性（大细胞性）贫血。孕早期叶酸水平不足会增加神经管缺陷（无脑畸形、spina bifida、脑膨出）的风险，孕前及孕早期补充叶酸可预防其中大部分，但不能预防全部。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 血清叶酸先下降，随后是红细胞叶酸。平均红细胞体积升高出现在贫血之前，血涂片可见中性粒细胞分叶过多。症状无特异性：疲劳、活动后气促、舌痛、口腔溃疡、轻度腹泻。妊娠期母体完全没有预警征象，神经管缺陷的首个证据通常来自胎儿畸形筛查超声。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 骨髓衰竭伴全血细胞减少、重度贫血、黏膜溃疡及吸收不良性腹泻。妊娠期的严重终点是结构性的：无脑畸形与生命不相容，开放性spina bifida会导致病灶平面以下终身瘫痪、脑积水以及肠道和膀胱功能障碍。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 血液学和黏膜方面的影响可完全逆转：网织红细胞增多在一周内开始出现，血细胞计数约两个月后恢复正常，不留残余缺陷。但已经形成的神经管缺陷是永久性的，之后任何摄入都无法逆转。神经管在受孕后26至28天闭合，因此妊娠试验阳性后才开始补充叶酸，对这一特定终点而言已经太晚，这正是主张在受孕前就开始补充的全部理由。
items.at_risk_zh: 有可能怀孕的女性，尤其是意外妊娠的情形。乳糜泻及其他吸收不良疾病。大量饮酒。干扰叶酸代谢的药物：甲氨蝶呤、柳氮磺吡啶、甲氧苄啶、苯妥英及其他抗惊厥药。慢性溶血和剥脱性皮肤病等细胞高周转状态。透析。
items.prevalence_zh: 在实行强制强化的美国，2011至2016年间，12至49岁女性中有18.6%的红细胞叶酸低于与神经管缺陷风险升高相关的阈值（748 nmol/L），低于2007至2010年的23.2%（PMID 31504109）。在强制强化的地区，典型的叶酸缺乏性贫血现已不常见，在未强化的地区则更常见。

items.function_short_zh: 为两种酶所必需：一种用于生成新血细胞，一种用于神经髓鞘的维护。
items.function_full_zh: 钴胺素是人体内恰好两种酶的辅因子。methionine synthase利用5-甲基四氢叶酸将同型半胱氨酸再甲基化为蛋氨酸，这一过程既能再生可用的叶酸，又能为维持髓鞘的甲基化反应提供S-腺苷蛋氨酸。methylmalonyl-CoA mutase在线粒体内催化甲基丙二酰辅酶A转化为琥珀酰辅酶A，参与奇数碳链脂肪酸和支链氨基酸的分解代谢。其吸收过程相当复杂：胃酸和胃蛋白酶将B12从食物蛋白中释放，壁细胞分泌的内因子负责转运，回肠末端的受体负责摄取。除严格素食饮食外，缺乏的常见原因是这条通路上某个环节出现故障，而非摄入不足。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 恶性贫血（自身免疫性内因子缺失）和脊髓亚急性联合变性，巨幼细胞性贫血是其血液学表现。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 甲基丙二酸和同型半胱氨酸的升高早于血清B12降至明确缺乏的范围，这也是临界结果常需复查这两项代谢物的原因。表现为手足对称性刺痛和麻木、振动觉和关节位置觉丧失、暗处更明显的步态不稳。还可见大细胞增多伴中性粒细胞分叶过多、舌痛且舌面光滑、疲劳、轻度认知迟缓和情绪低落。神经系统体征可以在全血细胞计数完全正常的情况下出现。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 脊髓亚急性联合变性：后索和皮质脊髓侧束脱髓鞘，导致感觉性共济失调、痉挛、跖反射阳性以及膀胱和肠道功能紊乱，未经治疗会进展为痉挛性截瘫并丧失独立行走能力。少数患者出现视神经萎缩，也有出现痴呆和精神病的。严重的巨幼细胞性贫血伴全血细胞减少也可能发生，但真正致残的是神经系统病变。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 血液学异常可完全纠正（一周内出现网织红细胞增多，计数约八周后恢复正常），但神经系统病变未必如此。在规模最大的一组病例系列中（143例患者共153次发作），47.1%的患者经治疗后神经系统异常完全恢复，6.3%遗留中度至重度残疾，也就是说多数接受治疗的患者可完全或接近完全恢复，少数人会留下残疾。治疗后残留的损害程度与治疗前缺陷的严重程度和持续时间成反比。恢复在最初两个月最快，可持续至约六个月。这正是为什么不明原因的大细胞性贫血绝不能盲目给予叶酸的原因：叶酸会修复血象、消除可见的信号，而脊髓损害仍在继续。
items.at_risk_zh: 60岁以上患有萎缩性胃炎、食物结合型B12吸收不良的成年人。自身免疫性恶性贫血患者。胃切除或胃旁路手术、回肠切除、克罗恩病患者。长期使用二甲双胍者。长期使用质子泵抑制剂或H2受体阻滞剂者。严格素食者，尤其重要的是其纯母乳喂养的婴儿。反复接触一氧化二氮者，无论是娱乐性还是职业性接触，这会直接使methionine synthase失活。
items.prevalence_zh: 美国和英国的大型调查显示，60岁及以上人群中约6%的血浆B12低于148 pmol/L，另有接近20%处于148至221 pmol/L的边缘范围，患病率随年龄增长而升高，且在低收入国家的各个年龄段都明显更高（PMID 19116323）。

items.function_short_zh: 维生素B6为多种氨基酸代谢酶提供动力，大剂量时则会损伤感觉神经。
items.function_full_zh: 活性形式5'-磷酸吡哆醛是100多种酶的辅因子，其中多数参与氨基酸代谢：转氨酶、合成血清素、多巴胺、GABA和组胺的脱羧酶、血红素合成的第一个限速步骤（ALA synthase）、glycogen phosphorylase，以及通过转硫途径清除同型半胱氨酸的cystathionine beta-synthase和gamma-lyase。需要量随蛋白质摄入量增加而上升。超过这些酶的饱和点后，额外补充的B6不再增加任何功能。大剂量产品（通常每日50至500 mg，用于经前症状、腕管综合征、妊娠恶心，或隐藏在复合B族维生素和能量补充剂中）反而会产生与剂量和持续时间相关的感觉神经病变，靶点是背根神经节。关于毒性问题，这与下文评定的缺乏症是两个不同的问题：由于损伤的是背根神经节内感觉神经元的胞体而非仅是轴突，停用补充剂后的恢复往往并不完全。麻木和位置觉障碍通常在数月内改善，有时改善明显，但部分人会遗留残余缺陷（Schaumburg 1983）。起病时间与剂量成反比，每日以克计的剂量可在数周内致病，而每日数十毫克则可能需要数年，这正是EFSA在2023年设定成人每日12 mg上限时，对50 mg/day参考点采用不确定系数4的原因。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 吡哆醇缺乏症：脂溢性皮炎伴口角炎和舌炎、低色素小细胞性贫血，以及婴儿癫痫发作，几乎总是继发于异烟肼、环丝氨酸、肼屈嗪或青霉胺、酒精依赖、透析或吸收不良。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 血浆5'-磷酸吡哆醛低于约20 nmol/L，通常完全没有症状。若出现症状，多为皮肤黏膜方面且无特异性：口角炎、舌炎、眼鼻口周围的脂溢性皮炎，加上易激惹和情绪低落。同型半胱氨酸可能轻度升高。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 血红素合成受损导致的低色素小细胞性贫血（不同于X连锁ALAS2基因相关的吡哆醇反应性铁粒幼细胞性贫血，后者是遗传性的，而非饮食性的），以及周围感觉神经病变。婴儿缺乏时会因GABA合成障碍而引发癫痫发作。单纯的重度缺乏很少见，几乎总是继发于：异烟肼、环丝氨酸、肼屈嗪或青霉胺治疗、酒精依赖、透析或吸收不良。需要注意的是，B6缺乏和过量都会导致周围神经病变，因此补充剂使用者出现的神经病变，由补充剂本身引起的可能性并不低于由其纠正的可能性。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 本字段评定的是缺乏症的恢复情况，适度补充数周内B6缺乏即可完全纠正，不留残余缺陷：皮肤黏膜体征消退，贫血缓解，给予维生素后吡哆醇反应性婴儿癫痫发作停止。大剂量B6神经病变的恢复是另一个问题，答案也不同（往往不完全），已在上文的功能描述中说明，此处不再重复。
items.at_risk_zh: 就缺乏而言：正在服用异烟肼、环丝氨酸、肼屈嗪或青霉胺者，酒精依赖者，透析患者，吸收不良患者。血浆PLP偏低也见于老年人、吸烟者以及正在或曾经使用口服避孕药者。就毒性而言：任何数月至数年服用大剂量B6或复合B族维生素产品的人，往往并未意识到摄入的剂量，因为单片药片就可能数倍超过欧洲的上限。
items.prevalence_zh: 在NHANES 2003至2004年调查中，未服用补充剂的美国成年人约有23%至27%血浆PLP低于20 nmol/L，多数只是生化指标异常而非有症状（PMID 18469270）。在毒性方面，EFSA于2023年将成人可耐受最高摄入量定为每日12 mg，其推导依据是外周神经病变的50 mg/day参考点，并采用不确定系数4（doi:10.2903/j.efsa.2023.8006）。

items.function_short_zh: 维持胶原蛋白强度和伤口愈合，缺乏时血管和牙龈会崩解。
items.function_full_zh: 抗坏血酸是一种还原型辅因子，负责维持一类双加氧酶中铁原子的活性状态。其中最知名的是prolyl-4-hydroxylase和lysyl hydroxylase，二者对胶原蛋白进行羟基化，使三螺旋结构稳定并能够交联；缺乏这两种酶时合成的胶原蛋白存在缺陷，这也解释了出血、伤口愈合不良和陈旧瘢痕重新裂开的原因。同样的化学机制还服务于dopamine beta-hydroxylase（去甲肾上腺素合成）、peptidylglycine alpha-amidating monooxygenase（肽类激素酰胺化）、两种参与肉碱生物合成的酶，以及基因调控中的HIF prolyl hydroxylases和TET、JmjC demethylases。抗坏血酸还能将膳食中的非血红素铁还原为可吸收的亚铁形式。人类无法自行合成维生素C，因为gulonolactone oxidase基因失活。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 摄入量低于约10 mg/day持续大约一到三个月后，血浆抗坏血酸下降，体内储存量降至约300 mg以下。第一阶段表现为疲劳、易激惹和大腿及小腿弥漫性酸痛，外观上没有可见改变。随后出现特征性皮肤体征：毛囊周围角化过度，大腿和胫部体毛呈螺旋状，毛囊周围出血，容易瘀伤，牙齿尚存者会出现牙龈肿胀、松软、出血。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 皮肤、肌肉和关节内出血，关节积血，以及骨膜下出血，后者在儿童中会引起严重肢体疼痛并拒绝活动（假性瘫痪）。陈旧的伤口和瘢痕会重新裂开，牙齿松动脱落，出现贫血和水肿。未经治疗的坏血病是致命的，通常死于出血或心力衰竭，不过在当前的医疗条件下，由于治疗极易获得，病情很少会发展到这一步。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 恢复完全且异常迅速。治疗开始后24至48小时内疲劳和疼痛就开始改善，牙龈出血和瘀伤在一到两周内消退，按每日100至300 mg补充，完全恢复大约需要三个月。不会遗留永久性缺陷，唯一的例外是已经脱落的牙齿，这不会再长回来。
items.at_risk_zh: 饮食中几乎不含水果蔬菜的人群：高度限制性或挑食者，包括部分自闭症儿童，独居的重度精神疾病或痴呆患者，酒精和药物依赖者，无家可归和食物不安全人群。此外还有吸烟者（需要量比一般人约高出35 mg/day）、透析患者、吸收不良患者，以及部分减重手术后患者。坏血病是一种饮食模式性疾病，而非补充剂摄入不足的问题，大约每日10 mg即可预防，一个橙子就能轻松超过这一需要量。
items.prevalence_zh: 在NHANES 2003至2004年调查中，美国6岁及以上人群有7.1%（标准误0.9）血清抗坏血酸低于11.4 micromol/L，低于NHANES III中约13%的水平，吸烟者和低收入群体的比例最高（PMID 19675106）。

items.supplement: High-dose folic acid plus B12 for cardiovascular prevention
items.supplement_zh: 大剂量叶酸联合维生素B12用于心血管预防
items.function_short_zh: 降低血液中的同型半胱氨酸，但结果证明并不能预防心肌梗死。
items.function_full_zh: 叶酸联合B12，常再加B6，能可靠地将血浆总同型半胱氨酸降低约四分之一，因为这两种维生素都为将同型半胱氨酸转回蛋氨酸的methionine synthase反应步骤提供底物。这一理论依据来自观察性研究：同型半胱氨酸升高与血管疾病和卒中相关。随机对照试验将这一生物标志物与疾病本身区分开来。该Cochrane综述总共纳入15项试验、71,422名受试者，各项结局分别汇总自这些试验中的一个子集：对心肌梗死无影响（7.1%对6.0%，RR 1.02，95% CI 0.95至1.10；12项试验，46,699名受试者），对全因死亡也无影响（11.7%对12.3%，RR 1.01，95% CI 0.96至1.06；11项试验，44,817名受试者），对卒中有小幅降低（4.3%对5.1%，RR 0.90，95% CI 0.82至0.99；10项试验，44,224名受试者），这一效应主要来自未实施叶酸强化、基线叶酸水平较低人群中的试验。有一个安全性问题延续自这两种成分本身：未先检查B12水平就给予大剂量叶酸，可能使B12缺乏引起的贫血指标恢复正常，而脊髓损害却在未被察觉的情况下继续进展，因此在给予这类剂量的叶酸之前，应先确认B12水平。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 不适用。这是一种针对心血管预防而检验的治疗方案，而非一种营养素。两种成分各自的缺乏状态见其各自的条目。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 不适用。复方制剂不存在其本身的缺乏状态。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 不适用。干预类别不存在缺乏状态。
items.at_risk_zh: 不适用。干预类别不存在缺乏状态。
items.prevalence_zh: 不适用。以下是效应量而非患病率：Cochrane推算出的需治疗人数（NNT）为143（95% CI 85至428），即5.4年内预防一次卒中所需治疗的人数，该数字来自叶酸联合依那普利的比较（CSPPT试验，研究对象为未实施叶酸强化的中国高血压人群），而非来自汇总10项试验的卒中效应估计值（PMID 28816346）。

items.function_short: Carries oxygen in the blood and powers the enzymes that turn food into usable energy.
items.function_full: Iron sits at the centre of the haem group in haemoglobin and myoglobin, where it binds and releases oxygen, and in the iron-sulfur clusters of mitochondrial complexes I to III, where it moves electrons during ATP synthesis. It is also the cofactor for ribonucleotide reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme of DNA synthesis, which is why dividing tissues (marrow, gut lining) fail first. In the developing brain it is required for tyrosine hydroxylase (dopamine synthesis), for oligodendrocyte myelination, and for hippocampal maturation, which is the mechanism behind the developmental findings in infants. Absorption is governed by hepcidin, and the direction runs opposite to what is often assumed: when stores are low hepcidin is suppressed, ferroportin survives on enterocytes and macrophages, and fractional absorption rises several-fold, from roughly 10% of intake to 20 to 30%. What hepcidin sets is the ceiling on rate, and there is no regulated route for excreting iron, so a large deficit still takes months to refill and oral iron works slowly. During inflammation hepcidin stays high and blocks absorption despite empty stores, which is why the anaemia of inflammation does not respond to oral iron.
items.deficiency_name: Iron deficiency anaemia (microcytic, hypochromic anaemia). Iron deficiency without anaemia is a recognised earlier stage of the same process.
items.deficiency_early: Serum ferritin falls long before haemoglobin does, so a blood test shows depleted stores while the full blood count is still normal. What a person notices at that stage: fatigue disproportionate to activity, breathlessness on stairs, cold hands, hair shedding, restless legs at night, and sometimes pica (craving ice or chalk). Ferritin is an acute-phase protein, so inflammation or infection can mask true depletion.
items.deficiency_severe: Haemoglobin falls with small pale red cells, producing pallor, tachycardia, exertional dyspnoea, and in extreme cases high-output cardiac failure. In pregnancy it raises the risk of preterm delivery, low birth weight, and poor infant iron stores. In infancy it impairs motor and cognitive development. In adults over 50 a new iron deficiency is a red flag for occult gastrointestinal bleeding and needs investigation rather than a supplement.
items.reversibility_note: In adults, anaemia and its symptoms correct fully once iron is replaced and the cause is fixed; haemoglobin typically rises within 4 to 8 weeks and stores refill over 3 to 6 months. Iron deficiency during infancy is the exception. Children with severe chronic iron deficiency in infancy still scored worse on cognitive, motor and behavioural measures more than 10 years after full iron treatment, so the developmental window matters more than the correction.
items.at_risk: Menstruating women, especially with heavy periods; pregnant women (requirement roughly doubles); infants 6 to 24 months, particularly preterm or low-birth-weight; frequent blood donors; endurance athletes; people with coeliac disease, inflammatory bowel disease, H. pylori gastritis or after bariatric surgery; vegetarian and vegan diets high in phytate; and anyone with chronic gastrointestinal blood loss.
items.prevalence: Anaemia affects about 33.7% of women aged 15 to 49 worldwide on GBD 2021 figures (age-standardised prevalence 33,716.77 per 100,000); WHO's 2019 estimates are lower, near 30% in non-pregnant women and 36 to 37% in pregnant women of that age band, about 29.9% overall. Iron deficiency is the single largest cause. In the US, the reported prevalence of iron deficiency in women depends on both the age band and the ferritin cut-off, which is why published figures disagree so widely: in females aged 12 to 21, ferritin below 25 micrograms/L gives about 38 to 39% (Weyand et al., JAMA 2023), while in a 62,685-woman US and Canadian sample of mean age 49.6 the same cut-off gives 15.33% and ferritin below 15 gives 7.43%; restricted to ages 25 to 54, three definitions span 4.46% to 21.23%.
items.source: Lozoff B, Jimenez E, Hagen J, Mollen E, Wolf AW. Pediatrics 2000;105(4):e51, PMID 10742372 (poorer behavioural and developmental outcome more than 10 years after treatment for iron deficiency in infancy); GBD 2021 anaemia analysis (age-standardised prevalence in women of reproductive age); WHO anaemia fact sheet and Global Health Observatory indicator (2019 estimates); Weyand AC et al., JAMA 2023;329(24):2191-2193, and 'Prevalence of Iron Deficiency Using 3 Definitions Among Women in the US and Canada', PMID 38848068; Camaschella C, N Engl J Med 2015;372:1832-1843.
corrections_applied: function_full: reversed the hepcidin claim. Deleted 'the body cannot simply take up more when stores are low' and replaced it with suppressed hepcidin, surviving ferroportin, and fractional absorption rising from roughly 10% to 20-30%; kept the two true constraints, no regulated excretion route (so refilling is rate-capped and slow) and high hepcidin during inflammation blocking uptake despite empty stores, which is why inflammatory anaemia does not respond to oral iron.

source: PMID 10742372 is Lozoff et al., Pediatrics 2000;105(4):e51, not Arch Pediatr Adolesc Med 2000;154:1108-1113. Replaced the journal, volume and page locator with the Pediatrics citation and the full author list.

prevalence: 33.7% is a GBD 2021 figure (33,716.77 per 100,000), not WHO GHO. Re-attributed it to GBD 2021 and stated WHO's 2019 numbers (about 30% non-pregnant, 36-37% pregnant, 29.9% overall) separately instead of blending the two sources.

prevalence: split the conflated '10% to 38%' US range by population. The 38-39% at ferritin below 25 now carries its age band (females 12-21, Weyand JAMA 2023); the adult figures now carry theirs (62,685-woman US/Canada sample, mean age 49.6: 7.43% at ferritin below 15, 15.33% at below 25; ages 25-54 spanning 4.46% to 21.23%).
source: added the Weyand JAMA 2023 and PMID 38848068 citations to support the newly split prevalence figures, plus the GBD 2021 attribution.

items.function_short: The raw material for thyroid hormone, which sets metabolic rate and builds the fetal brain.
items.function_full: Iodine has exactly one job: it is the substrate thyroid peroxidase attaches to tyrosine residues on thyroglobulin to make thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3). There is no alternative pathway and no substitute element. T3 acting on nuclear thyroid hormone receptors drives basal metabolic rate and thermogenesis in adults. In the fetus it governs neuronal migration, dendritic branching, synaptogenesis and myelination, on a fixed developmental timetable. The fetal thyroid does not begin producing hormone until roughly week 12 to 16, so first-trimester brain development runs entirely on maternal T4 crossing the placenta. Maternal requirement rises to about 250 micrograms per day in pregnancy and lactation.
items.deficiency_name: Iodine deficiency disorders: endemic goitre and hypothyroidism in adults, and endemic cretinism as the severe congenital form.
items.deficiency_early: The thyroid enlarges (goitre) as TSH rises to extract more iodine from a falling supply. On testing, a population median urinary iodine concentration below 100 micrograms/L (below 150 in pregnancy) and a raised serum thyroglobulin signal inadequacy before any clinical change. A pregnant woman with mild to moderate deficiency usually notices nothing at all, which is what makes this dangerous.
items.deficiency_severe: Endemic cretinism: severe intellectual disability, deaf-mutism, spastic diplegia and stunted growth in a child whose mother was severely deficient during pregnancy. Adults develop overt hypothyroidism with cold intolerance, weight gain, bradycardia and, in extreme untreated cases, myxoedema. Even mild to moderate maternal deficiency is associated with lower verbal IQ and reading scores in the child, on the order of a few points, which is small individually and large across a population.
items.reversibility_note: Goitre, adult hypothyroidism and impaired thyroid function correct with iodine repletion. Brain damage sustained in utero and in the first two years of life does not. The window is narrower than the whole pregnancy but far wider than the moment a pregnancy is confirmed: in Cao's trial, iodine given in the first or second trimester left 2% of infants with moderate or severe neurologic abnormality, against 9% when it was given in the third trimester or after birth, so treatment up to the end of the second trimester still protects the fetal brain. Beyond that window iodine given to an affected child undoes nothing; only iodine reaching the mother in time prevents the damage. The practical reading is to start immediately, not to conclude it is too late. This is the strongest irreversibility case among common micronutrients, and the reason salt iodisation is a public health programme rather than an individual choice.
items.at_risk: Pregnant and lactating women anywhere, since requirements rise sharply. Populations in iodine-poor soil regions (mountainous and flood-plain areas) without salt iodisation. People who avoid iodised salt while also avoiding dairy, eggs and seafood, including strict vegans without a deliberate iodine source. Users of non-iodised speciality salts (pink, sea, kosher), which supply essentially no iodine.
items.prevalence: 21 countries still had insufficient population iodine intake as of 2020-2021, down from 113 in 1993, thanks to salt iodisation (IGN Global Scorecard of Iodine Nutrition). Mild to moderate deficiency in pregnant women persists in countries whose general populations are replete, including the UK, Norway and Australia. Iodine deficiency remains the leading preventable cause of intellectual disability worldwide.
items.source: Cao XY et al., N Engl J Med 1994;331:1739-1744, doi:10.1056/NEJM199412293312603, PMID 7984194 (timing of iodine treatment in pregnancy and neurologic outcome in the child); Hetzel BS, 'Iodine deficiency and fetal brain damage', N Engl J Med 1994;331:1770-1771, doi:10.1056/NEJM199412293312610, PMID 7984200 (accompanying editorial); Bath SC et al., Lancet 2013;382:331-337 (mild maternal deficiency and child IQ, ALSPAC); Iodine Global Network, Global Scorecard of Iodine Nutrition, ign.org/scorecard; Zimmermann MB, Lancet 2008;372:1251-1262.
corrections_applied: reversibility_note: removed 'The first-trimester component of the damage is already fixed by the time a pregnancy is confirmed', which the companion trial to the entry's own cited editorial contradicts. Replaced it with Cao's finding (2% moderate or severe neurologic abnormality with first- or second-trimester iodine versus 9% in the third trimester or after birth) and the correct window, closing around the end of the second trimester. Changed the practical conclusion from 'too late' to 'start immediately'.
reversibility: left IRREVERSIBLE unchanged, as the checker confirmed the classification is correct.

source: N Engl J Med 1994;331:1770-1771 is Hetzel's editorial (PMID 7984200), not a Delange paper. Removed the Delange attribution, cited the primary Cao trial as the lead source, and kept the Hetzel editorial correctly attributed.

items.function_short: Zinc runs hundreds of enzymes; the lozenge form targets cold symptoms in the throat.
items.function_full: Zinc is a structural or catalytic component of more than 300 enzymes and of the roughly 2,000 zinc-finger transcription factors that bind DNA, so it is required for gene expression, DNA and RNA synthesis, and cell division. Tissues with fast turnover fail first: gut mucosa, skin, growth plate cartilage, and lymphocytes. Thymic function and T-cell development are zinc-dependent, which is the basis of the immune effects. The lozenge specifically is a different proposition from nutrition: it works (where it works) by releasing ionic zinc onto the oropharyngeal mucosa, where it appears to interfere with rhinovirus replication and ICAM-1 binding locally. That is a short-course pharmacological use in someone whose zinc status is usually normal. Lozenges are a poor way to correct systemic deficiency. On the toxicity side, sustained intake above the 40 mg/day tolerable upper limit induces intestinal metallothionein and progressively impairs copper status; the upper limit itself rests on a marginal fall in erythrocyte superoxide dismutase at around 60 mg/day, a biochemical rather than a clinical endpoint. Frank copper-deficiency anaemia and myeloneuropathy are reported at prolonged intakes several times higher, in the region of 100 to 300 mg/day, typically from high-dose supplements or zinc-containing denture cream.
items.deficiency_name: Nutritional zinc deficiency (growth failure, chronic diarrhoea, impaired immunity, characteristic dermatitis). Acrodermatitis enteropathica is the inherited form, caused by SLC39A4 mutations impairing zinc uptake, and is a genetic disorder rather than a consequence of diet.
items.deficiency_early: Blunted taste and smell, poor appetite, slow wound healing, and infections that are more frequent and last longer. In children, growth velocity crosses centiles downward before any skin change appears. There is no good early biomarker: plasma zinc falls only late, drops during any inflammatory episode, and varies with time of day and recent meals, so a normal plasma zinc does not exclude deficiency.
items.deficiency_severe: Stunting and delayed sexual maturation in children, persistent diarrhoea that worsens the deficiency in a loop, alopecia, and a distinctive bullous, crusted dermatitis around the mouth, eyes, genitals and on the hands and feet. Cell-mediated immunity is impaired, with thymic atrophy and reduced T-cell counts. In young children in low-income settings, zinc deficiency contributes measurably to deaths from diarrhoeal disease and pneumonia.
items.reversibility_note: Dermatitis, taste disturbance, diarrhoea and immune function recover within days to a few weeks of repletion, and the response is often dramatic. Linear growth is the part that does not fully catch up: height lost during a prolonged deficiency spanning a growth period is only partly recovered, and final adult stature can remain reduced.
items.at_risk: People on cereal-based diets high in phytate with little animal protein, which is the dominant global pattern. Children in low-income settings. Malabsorption from Crohn's disease, coeliac disease or short bowel; bariatric surgery. Chronic alcohol use, which causes urinary zinc loss. Chronic diarrhoea, sickle cell disease, and older adults with restricted intake. High-dose supplemental iron taken at the same time competes for the same absorptive route.
items.prevalence: An estimated 17.3% of the world's population is at risk of inadequate zinc intake, based on national food-supply zinc availability (Wessells and Brown, 2012). Clinically overt nutritional zinc deficiency in healthy adults in high-income countries is uncommon.
items.source: Wessells KR, Brown KH. PLoS One 2012;7:e50568, PMID 23209782; King JC et al., J Nutr 2016;146:858S-885S (IZiNCG biomarkers); Hemila H et al., Br J Clin Pharmacol 2016;82:1393-1398 (individual patient data meta-analysis, zinc acetate lozenges and common cold duration); Hemila H, JRSM Open 2017;8(5):2054270417694291 (zinc acetate versus gluconate and dose); NIH Office of Dietary Supplements, Zinc Fact Sheet for Health Professionals (UL 40 mg/d, basis and copper interaction).
corrections_applied: function_full: de-overstated the copper threshold. 'Above roughly 40 mg/day ... causes copper deficiency with anaemia and myelopathy' became progressive impairment of copper status above the 40 mg/day upper limit, with the note that the UL rests on a marginal erythrocyte superoxide dismutase fall around 60 mg/day, and frank copper-deficiency anaemia and myeloneuropathy placed at prolonged intakes of roughly 100 to 300 mg/day from high-dose supplements or denture cream.

source: BMJ Open 2017;7:e013295 is Mohn et al., a type 1 diabetes emotional-distress pilot study, unrelated to zinc or colds. Removed it and substituted Hemila's actual lozenge evidence, Br J Clin Pharmacol 2016;82:1393-1398 and JRSM Open 2017;8(5):2054270417694291.
reversibility: left as PARTIAL describing recovery from the deficiency; the toxicity material sits in function_full prose, not in the reversibility field.

items.function_short: Selenium builds the enzymes that mop up oxidative damage and switch on thyroid hormone.
items.function_full: Selenium is incorporated as the amino acid selenocysteine into about 25 human selenoproteins. The glutathione peroxidases (GPX1 to GPX4) reduce hydrogen peroxide and lipid hydroperoxides, GPX4 specifically preventing ferroptotic membrane damage. Thioredoxin reductases maintain cellular redox state and support DNA synthesis. The iodothyronine deiodinases convert T4 to active T3, which links selenium status to thyroid function. Selenoprotein P is the plasma transport form and the best status marker. The dose in this entry matters. Plasma glutathione peroxidase (GPX3) plateaus near 55 micrograms per day, which is what the RDA is built on. Selenoprotein P plateaus somewhere in the range of roughly 50 to 105 micrograms per day depending on baseline status: about 49 micrograms per day in selenium-deficient Chinese subjects, against about 105 micrograms per day of total intake in UK adults (a 50 microgram supplement on top of roughly 55 micrograms habitual). Either way, 200 micrograms per day supplies three to four times the adult RDA and produces no further enzyme activity in someone already replete, while sitting halfway to the tolerable upper limit of 400 micrograms per day.
