In the Nutritional Prevention of Cancer trial, 200 micrograms per day for a mean 7.7 years raised type 2 diabetes incidence (hazard ratio 1.55, 95% CI 1.03 to 2.33), concentrated in participants who started in the highest baseline selenium tertile (hazard ratio 2.70).
items.deficiency_name: Keshan disease, an endemic cardiomyopathy. Kashin-Beck disease, an endemic osteoarthropathy, occurs in the same low-selenium regions and is associated with, though not fully explained by, selenium deficiency.
items.deficiency_early: Plasma selenium and glutathione peroxidase activity fall with no symptoms at all. In endemic areas, subclinical ECG abnormalities and reduced ejection fraction appear before overt illness, which is how latent Keshan disease is detected on screening. Isolated cases outside endemic areas typically surface as unexplained myopathy, muscle pain, or whitened nail beds.
items.deficiency_severe: Keshan disease presents acutely with cardiogenic shock and arrhythmia, or chronically as congestive cardiomyopathy with cardiac enlargement and multifocal myocardial necrosis and fibrosis. It classically strikes children and women of childbearing age in low-soil-selenium areas and is fatal without treatment. A coxsackievirus co-factor is thought to trigger the acute form in a selenium-depleted host. Kashin-Beck disease destroys growth-plate and articular cartilage, producing shortened fingers, deformed ankles, knees, wrists and elbows, and permanently limited movement.
items.reversibility_note: Early Keshan disease responds well to selenium replacement, and heart failure can improve substantially or resolve if caught before the myocardium is remodelled. Once dilated cardiomyopathy with established fibrosis has developed, the myocardial damage does not fully reverse and outcomes are poor. Kashin-Beck cartilage necrosis and the resulting joint deformity are permanent. Prophylactic sodium selenite in endemic Chinese counties prevented new cases, which is the clearest evidence the causal direction is right.
items.at_risk: Residents of low-selenium soil belts, chiefly the diagonal band across China from the northeast to the southwest, plus parts of Siberia. Long-term parenteral nutrition without added selenium. Severe malabsorption, short bowel, and cystic fibrosis. Dialysis patients. Dietary selenium deficiency is not a realistic concern for anyone eating a mixed diet in North America, where soil selenium is high; two Brazil nuts alone exceed the adult RDA.
items.prevalence: NOT ESTABLISHED as a current global figure. Keshan disease was endemic across a defined low-selenium region of China and has been reduced to near-zero incidence since selenite supplementation and food-supply changes began in the 1970s. Dietary selenium deficiency is essentially absent in the United States, where median intake already exceeds the RDA from food alone.
items.source: Stranges S et al., Ann Intern Med 2007;147:217-223, PMID 17620655 (200 µg/d and type 2 diabetes, NPC trial); Hurst R et al., Am J Clin Nutr 2010, 'Establishing optimal selenium status', PMID 20181815 (selenoprotein P plateau in UK adults); Xia Y et al., selenoprotein P optimisation in selenium-deficient Chinese subjects, PMC2921536; Rayman MP, Lancet 2012;379:1256-1268; Keshan Disease, StatPearls, NCBI Bookshelf NBK603722; Institute of Medicine DRI for selenium (RDA 55 µg/d, UL 400 µg/d).
corrections_applied: function_full: separated the two plateaus that were collapsed into 'roughly 55 to 75 micrograms per day'. GPX3 now plateaus near 55 micrograms per day (the RDA basis), and selenoprotein P is quoted at roughly 50 to 105 micrograms per day depending on baseline status, with both endpoints named (about 49 in selenium-deficient Chinese subjects, about 105 total intake in UK adults).

function_full: kept the argument that 200 micrograms per day adds no enzyme activity in a replete person, which the checker confirmed is unaffected by the correction, and kept the NPC trial figures the checker verified as correct.
source: added Hurst et al. (PMID 20181815) and Xia et al. (PMC2921536) to support the revised plateau range.

items.function_short: A cofactor in hundreds of reactions; every molecule of ATP works bound to magnesium.
items.function_full: The biologically active form of ATP is Mg-ATP, so magnesium is an obligate participant in every kinase reaction, every ATPase and both DNA and RNA polymerases, more than 300 enzymes in total. It acts as a physiological calcium antagonist: it blocks the NMDA receptor channel at rest and dampens calcium entry in vascular smooth muscle and myocardium, which is why depletion raises neuromuscular excitability and arrhythmia risk. Magnesium is also required both for parathyroid hormone secretion and for end-organ response to it, so depletion produces a hypocalcaemia that will not correct until magnesium is replaced. About 60% of body magnesium is locked in bone and most of the rest is intracellular, leaving only about 1% in serum. Serum magnesium is therefore a poor guide to total body status and can be normal in a genuinely depleted person.
items.deficiency_name: Symptomatic hypomagnesaemia (ICD-10 E83.4). There is no eponymous deficiency disease; the severe presentation is hypomagnesaemic tetany with refractory hypocalcaemia and hypokalaemia. Inherited renal magnesium wasting (Gitelman syndrome, familial hypomagnesaemia with hypercalciuria) is a genetic tubular disorder rather than a dietary deficiency.
items.deficiency_early: Usually nothing at all. Low dietary intake shows up as intake below the estimated average requirement with a normal serum magnesium, because the kidney conserves aggressively. The first things a person notices are muscle cramps, eyelid or hand tremor, and irritability or poor sleep, all of which are non-specific. In practice a low serum magnesium is most often spotted incidentally on a metabolic panel run for unexplained hypokalaemia or hypocalcaemia.
items.deficiency_severe: Tetany with positive Chvostek and Trousseau signs, paraesthesiae, seizures, and cardiac arrhythmias including atrial fibrillation and torsades de pointes. Accompanying hypokalaemia and hypocalcaemia resist correction until magnesium itself is replaced, which is the clinically important teaching point. Severe cases are almost always driven by drug or gastrointestinal or renal losses rather than by diet alone.
items.reversibility_note: Repletion corrects the neuromuscular and cardiac features and allows the linked potassium and calcium abnormalities to correct, with no residual deficit once the underlying cause is addressed. The one caveat is timing rather than permanence: serum magnesium normalises before body stores do, so bone and intracellular pools take days to weeks to refill and stopping too early lets the deficit return.
items.at_risk: Chronic alcohol use, one of the leading causes. Gastrointestinal losses from chronic diarrhoea, malabsorption, short bowel and after bariatric surgery, together with renal losses, account for a large share of clinically encountered hypomagnesaemia. Long-term proton pump inhibitor use, which can cause profound hypomagnesaemia. Loop and thiazide diuretics, cisplatin, amphotericin, and calcineurin inhibitors; drug causes dominate in hospital populations. Poorly controlled diabetes with osmotic diuresis. Refeeding syndrome. In someone with normal kidneys and a normal gut, diet alone rarely produces symptomatic deficiency.
items.prevalence: About 48% of Americans of all ages consume less magnesium from food and beverages than their estimated average requirement (NHANES 2013-2016). Clinically significant hypomagnesaemia is less common than that figure suggests: roughly 2.5% to 15% in the general population, rising to about 10% to 20% of hospitalised patients and higher in intensive care. The gap between the intake figure and the clinical one is why low intake is often overstated as widespread deficiency.
items.source: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements, Magnesium Health Professional Fact Sheet, ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Magnesium-HealthProfessional (NHANES 2013-2016 intake data); Ayuk J, Gittoes NJL, Ann Clin Biochem 2014;51:179-188, PMID 24402002 (contemporary view of hypomagnesaemia; 2.5-15% general population); Gragossian A et al., Hypomagnesemia, StatPearls, NCBI Bookshelf NBK500003.
corrections_applied: prevalence: raised 'roughly 2%' to the cited source's actual 2.5% to 15% general-population range, and dropped 'far' from 'far less common' since the gap between intake shortfall and clinical deficiency narrows once the correct range is used. The underlying point that low intake is not the same as clinical deficiency is kept, not softened.

at_risk: removed the unsupported ranking claim 'the single most common cause' from chronic alcohol use, listing it among the leading causes instead, and added the gastrointestinal, renal and drug causes that account for a large share of clinically encountered hypomagnesaemia, with drug causes noted as dominant in hospital populations.
source: added PMID 24402002 to the Ayuk and Gittoes citation and tagged it with the 2.5-15% figure it supports.

items.supplement: Calcium supplements on top of an adequate diet
items.function_short: Builds bone mineral and carries the signals for muscle contraction, nerve firing and clotting.
items.function_full: About 99% of body calcium is hydroxyapatite crystal in bone and teeth, serving a structural role. The remaining 1% is the cell's universal second messenger: it triggers excitation-contraction coupling in muscle, neurotransmitter release at synapses, and several steps of the coagulation cascade. Serum ionised calcium is defended within a very narrow range by parathyroid hormone, calcitriol and bone resorption, so a low dietary intake does not lower blood calcium. It is paid for out of the skeleton instead. That regulation is the key to this particular entry. Fractional absorption falls as intake rises, so in a person already meeting requirements from food, additional supplemental calcium contributes little to bone mineral and the surplus is largely excreted. What a supplement does add that food does not is a large absorptive bolus, and that is the context for the constipation, the increased kidney stone risk seen in the Women's Health Initiative, and the contested cardiovascular signal.
items.deficiency_name: Calcium-deficiency rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults, with nutritional secondary hyperparathyroidism. This is a disease of genuinely low intake and has no bearing on whether someone eating an adequate diet adds a supplement.
items.deficiency_early: Nothing a person notices. Biochemically, parathyroid hormone rises while serum calcium stays normal, urinary calcium falls, and bone turnover markers climb. The skeleton is being drawn on silently, which is why the early phase is only ever detected on testing done for another reason.
items.deficiency_severe: In children, rickets with bowed legs, widened wrists and costochondral junctions, bone pain and delayed growth. In adults, osteomalacia with diffuse bone pain, proximal muscle weakness and pseudofractures, and over decades accelerated bone loss with increased fragility fracture risk. Symptomatic hypocalcaemia with tetany and paraesthesiae comes from parathyroid or vitamin D failure rather than from dietary shortfall alone, because the skeleton buffers intake so effectively.
items.reversibility_note: Rickets and osteomalacia heal with calcium repletion (plus vitamin D where that is also deficient), and bone mineral density largely restores. Two things do not fully recover: skeletal deformity already established in a growing child, along with the height lost to it, and peak bone mass never accrued during adolescence, which sets the lifetime baseline and cannot be rebuilt later by supplementing.
items.at_risk: Children on low-calcium, high-phytate diets in parts of sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia, where dietary intakes around 200 mg/day have been documented. Adults with no dairy and no fortified alternatives. Malabsorption, post-gastrectomy states, long-term corticosteroid use, and untreated coeliac disease. The population this entry describes, someone whose diet already meets requirements, is not at risk by definition, which is the whole point.
items.prevalence: NOT ESTABLISHED as a global figure for calcium-specific deficiency, because it is difficult to separate from vitamin D deficiency in survey data. Regionally it is well documented: median dietary calcium intake in Nigerian children with nutritional rickets was about 203 mg/day, against 196 mg/day in controls (P=0.64), on a requirement of roughly 700 to 1,300 mg/day depending on age. Calcium alone outperformed vitamin D alone in treating them, with 61% on calcium and 58% on the combination reaching the combined endpoint against 19% on vitamin D alone.
items.source: Thacher TD et al., N Engl J Med 1999;341:563-568, PMID 10451461 (calcium vs vitamin D for nutritional rickets; median intake 203 mg/day in cases, 196 mg/day in controls); Institute of Medicine, Dietary Reference Intakes for Calcium and Vitamin D, 2011, doi:10.17226/13050; Jackson RD et al., N Engl J Med 2006;354:669-683 (WHI: calcium plus vitamin D, fracture and renal stone outcomes).
corrections_applied: prevalence: the cited trial reports no 217 mg/day and no mean. Replaced with Thacher's actual median of about 203 mg/day in the children with rickets, and added the control value of 196 mg/day (P=0.64) that the correction supplies.
prevalence: kept the calcium-beats-vitamin-D claim, which the checker verified, and attached its supporting numbers (61% calcium, 58% combination, 19% vitamin D alone reaching the combined endpoint).
source: annotated the Thacher citation with the corrected median figures.

items.function_short: Not a nutrient. Gut and mouth bacteria turn it into nitric oxide, which widens blood vessels.
items.function_full: Inorganic nitrate from beetroot and leafy greens is absorbed in the proximal small intestine, and roughly a quarter of the circulating pool is actively concentrated by the salivary glands. Commensal bacteria on the posterior tongue reduce it to nitrite, and swallowed nitrite is further reduced to nitric oxide in the acidic stomach and in hypoxic tissue by deoxyhaemoglobin, deoxymyoglobin, xanthine oxidoreductase and other metalloproteins. This enterosalivary route is a supplementary supply line that runs in parallel with the body's own synthesis of nitric oxide from L-arginine by nitric oxide synthase, which is the primary and always-available pathway. That distinction is what makes nitrate a usable substrate rather than a required nutrient: NOS-derived nitric oxide continues normally on a nitrate-free diet. Measured effects are pharmacological and dose-dependent: vasodilation with a modest fall in blood pressure, and a reduced oxygen cost of submaximal exercise. Antibacterial mouthwash abolishes the effect entirely by killing the nitrate-reducing oral flora, which is the clearest demonstration that the mechanism is microbial rather than nutritional.
items.at_risk: NOT APPLICABLE. No one becomes deficient in dietary nitrate, because the body has no requirement for it and synthesises nitric oxide independently. A person eating no beetroot and no leafy greens has lower plasma nitrite and forgoes the blood pressure and exercise-economy effects, which is a missed pharmacological benefit rather than a deficiency state.
items.prevalence: NOT APPLICABLE. Dietary nitrate is not an essential nutrient and has no deficiency state, so no prevalence figure exists and none should be quoted. For scale of the effect rather than of a deficiency, pooled trials report systolic blood pressure reductions of roughly 3 to 5 mmHg, largest in hypertensive participants.
items.source: Lundberg JO, Weitzberg E, Gladwin MT. Nat Rev Drug Discov 2008;7:156-167, doi:10.1038/nrd2466 (nitrate-nitrite-nitric oxide pathway); Siervo M et al., J Nutr 2013;143:818-826, PMID 23596162 (beetroot juice and blood pressure, pooled systolic reduction 4.4 mmHg); Jackson JK et al., Nutr Rev 2018;76(5):348-371, doi:10.1093/nutrit/nuy005, PMID 29506204 (inorganic nitrate and nitrite, cardiovascular risk factors, systematic review and meta-analysis); Govoni M et al., Nitric Oxide 2008;19:333-337 (antibacterial mouthwash abolishes the effect).
corrections_applied: source: 'Jackson JK et al., J Nutr 2018;148:1749-1762' does not resolve. Replaced the locator with the real Jackson JK meta-analysis, Nutr Rev 2018;76(5):348-371, doi 10.1093/nutrit/nuy005, PMID 29506204, and added Siervo M et al., J Nutr 2013;143:818-826 (PMID 23596162) as the specific pooled beetroot blood pressure estimate behind the 3 to 5 mmHg figure.
prevalence: kept the 3 to 5 mmHg number, which the checker confirmed is well supported; only the citation was wrong.

classification: NONE / NA left untouched. Consistency verified: deficiency_name NONE, deficiency_early and deficiency_severe NOT APPLICABLE, reversibility NA with reversibility_note NOT APPLICABLE, and at_risk and prevalence both open with NOT APPLICABLE before explaining why no deficiency state exists.

items.function_short_zh: 铁负责在血液中运输氧气,并驱动把食物转化为可用能量的酶系统。
items.function_full_zh: 铁位于血红蛋白和肌红蛋白血红素基团的中心,负责结合和释放氧气,也存在于线粒体复合体I至III的铁硫簇中,负责在ATP合成过程中传递电子。铁还是ribonucleotide reductase(核糖核苷酸还原酶,DNA合成的限速酶)的辅因子,这就是为何增殖旺盛的组织(骨髓、肠道黏膜)最先受累。在发育中的大脑里,铁是tyrosine hydroxylase(酪氨酸羟化酶,负责多巴胺合成)、少突胶质细胞髓鞘形成以及海马成熟所必需的,这正是婴儿发育相关研究结果背后的机制。铁的吸收受hepcidin(铁调素)调控,其作用方向与常见的误解相反:当体内铁储备低时,铁调素受到抑制,肠上皮细胞和巨噬细胞上的ferroportin(膜铁转运蛋白)得以留存,吸收分数随之成倍上升,从摄入量的约10%升至20%至30%。铁调素设定的是吸收速率的上限,而人体没有可调节的排铁途径,因此大量的铁缺口仍需数月才能补足,口服铁剂起效缓慢。炎症状态下铁调素持续处于高水平,即使铁储备已经耗尽仍会阻断吸收,这就是炎症性贫血对口服铁剂无反应的原因。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 缺铁性贫血(小细胞低色素性贫血)。不伴贫血的缺铁是同一病理过程公认的更早期阶段。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 血清铁蛋白的下降远早于血红蛋白,因此血液检查可显示铁储备已耗竭,而全血细胞计数仍正常。此阶段患者可能察觉到的表现包括:与活动量不相称的疲劳、爬楼梯气短、手脚发凉、脱发、夜间不宁腿,有时还有异食癖(嗜食冰块或粉笔)。铁蛋白是一种急性期蛋白,因此炎症或感染可能掩盖真实的铁储备耗竭。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 血红蛋白下降,红细胞变小变淡,导致面色苍白、心动过速、活动后呼吸困难,极端情况下可出现高排量心力衰竭。孕期缺铁会增加早产、低出生体重及婴儿铁储备不足的风险。婴儿期缺铁会损害运动和认知发育。50岁以上成人新发缺铁是隐匿性消化道出血的警示信号,应及时检查,不应仅仅补充铁剂。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 在成人中,一旦补铁并纠正病因,贫血及其症状可完全恢复:血红蛋白通常在4至8周内回升,铁储备在3至6个月内补足。婴儿期缺铁是例外。婴儿期曾患严重慢性缺铁的儿童,在接受充分铁剂治疗10年以上后,认知、运动和行为测评得分依然较差,说明发育窗口期比纠正本身更为关键。
items.at_risk_zh: 处于月经期的女性,尤其是月经量大者;孕妇(需求量约增加一倍);6至24个月龄的婴儿,尤其是早产儿或低出生体重儿;频繁献血者;耐力运动员;患有乳糜泻、炎症性肠病、H. pylori胃炎或接受减重手术后的人群;富含植酸的素食及纯素饮食者;以及任何存在慢性消化道失血的人。
items.prevalence_zh: 根据GBD 2021数据,全球15至49岁女性中约33.7%患贫血(年龄标准化患病率33,716.77/100,000);世卫组织2019年的估计值较低,非孕妇约30%,同龄段孕妇为36%至37%,总体约29.9%。缺铁是贫血最主要的单一病因。在美国,女性缺铁患病率的报告数字取决于年龄段和铁蛋白临界值,这也是各项发表数据差异巨大的原因:在12至21岁女性中,铁蛋白低于25微克/升时患病率约为38%至39%(Weyand等,JAMA 2023);而在一项62,685名美国和加拿大女性、平均年龄49.6岁的样本中,同一临界值下患病率为15.33%,铁蛋白低于15时为7.43%;若限定在25至54岁,三种定义下的患病率范围为4.46%至21.23%。

items.function_short_zh: 甲状腺激素的原料,决定代谢率并构建胎儿大脑。
items.function_full_zh: 碘只有一项功能:作为thyroid peroxidase(甲状腺过氧化物酶)连接到甲状腺球蛋白酪氨酸残基上的底物,用以合成甲状腺素(T4)和三碘甲状腺原氨酸(T3)。没有替代通路,也没有可替代的元素。T3作用于核甲状腺激素受体,驱动成人的基础代谢率和产热。在胎儿体内,碘按固定的发育时间表调控神经元迁移、树突分支、突触形成和髓鞘化。胎儿甲状腺大约要到第12至16周才开始分泌激素,因此妊娠早期的大脑发育完全依赖经胎盘进入的母体T4。孕期和哺乳期母体需求量升至每日约250微克。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 碘缺乏病:成人表现为地方性甲状腺肿和甲状腺功能减退,严重的先天型为地方性克汀病。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 随着促甲状腺激素(TSH)升高以从减少的供应中提取更多碘,甲状腺会增大(甲状腺肿)。在检测层面,人群尿碘浓度中位数低于100微克/升(孕期低于150)以及血清甲状腺球蛋白升高,会在出现任何临床变化之前就提示碘摄入不足。轻中度缺碘的孕妇通常毫无察觉,这正是其危险所在。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 地方性克汀病:母亲孕期严重缺碘的孩子会出现重度智力障碍、聋哑、痉挛性双侧瘫和生长迟缓。成人则出现明显的甲状腺功能减退,表现为怕冷、体重增加、心动过缓,极端未治疗病例可出现黏液性水肿。即使母体只是轻中度缺碘,孩子的言语智商和阅读成绩也会降低,幅度为几分,个体层面看幅度不大,但放到人群层面影响显著。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 甲状腺肿、成人甲状腺功能减退及甲状腺功能受损,在补碘后可以纠正。子宫内及出生后头两年内造成的脑损伤则不能。这个窗口期比整个孕期窄,但远比确认怀孕的那一刻宽:在Cao的试验中,妊娠早期或中期补碘的婴儿中有2%出现中度或重度神经系统异常,而妊娠晚期或出生后才补碘的比例为9%,说明在妊娠中期结束前进行治疗仍能保护胎儿大脑。超过这一窗口期后,给患儿补碘无法逆转已造成的损害,只有及时让碘到达母体才能预防损害。实际的启示是应立即开始补碘,而不是认为为时已晚。这是常见微量营养素中不可逆性证据最强的一例,也是食盐加碘作为公共卫生项目而非个人选择的原因。
items.at_risk_zh: 任何地方的孕妇和哺乳期女性,因为需求量急剧上升。土壤缺碘地区(山区和洪泛平原地区)且未实行食盐加碘的人群。既不使用加碘盐、又同时不摄入乳制品、鸡蛋和海鲜的人,包括未刻意补充碘来源的严格素食者。使用非加碘特种盐(粉盐、海盐、犹太盐)的人,这类盐基本不含碘。
items.prevalence_zh: 截至2020至2021年,仍有21个国家人群碘摄入不足,得益于食盐加碘,这一数字已从1993年的113个下降(IGN全球碘营养记分卡)。在英国、挪威、澳大利亚等一般人群碘充足的国家,孕妇轻中度缺碘依然存在。碘缺乏仍是全球可预防性智力障碍的首要病因。

items.function_short_zh: 锌驱动数百种酶;含片剂型则针对咽喉部的感冒症状。
items.function_full_zh: 锌是300多种酶的结构或催化成分,也是约2,000种结合DNA的锌指(zinc finger)转录因子的组成部分,因此是基因表达、DNA和RNA合成以及细胞分裂所必需的。更新速度快的组织最先受累:肠黏膜、皮肤、生长板软骨和淋巴细胞。胸腺功能和T细胞发育依赖锌,这是其免疫作用的基础。锌含片本身是与营养补充不同的用法:它(在起效时)通过向口咽黏膜释放离子锌发挥作用,在局部似乎能干扰鼻病毒(rhinovirus)复制及其与ICAM-1的结合。这是一种针对锌状态通常正常者的短程药理学用法。含片并不是纠正全身性缺锌的良好方式。在毒性方面,长期摄入超过每日40毫克的可耐受最高摄入量会诱导肠道金属硫蛋白(metallothionein)生成,并逐渐损害铜的状态;这一上限本身依据的是每日约60毫克摄入时红细胞超氧化物歧化酶(superoxide dismutase)出现的轻微下降,这是一个生化终点,不是临床终点。明显的铜缺乏性贫血和脊髓神经病变见于长期摄入量高出数倍、约每日100至300毫克的情况,通常来自高剂量补充剂或含锌义齿粘合剂。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 营养性缺锌(生长发育不良、慢性腹泻、免疫功能受损、特征性皮炎)。Acrodermatitis enteropathica(肠病性肢端皮炎)是其遗传性形式,由SLC39A4基因突变导致锌摄取受损引起。这是一种遗传性疾病,不是饮食因素造成的。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 味觉和嗅觉减退、食欲不振、伤口愈合缓慢,以及感染更频繁且病程更长。在儿童中,生长速度会先跨百分位曲线下降,之后才出现皮肤改变。目前没有良好的早期生物标志物:血浆锌只有在晚期才下降,任何炎症发作期间都会降低,并随一天中的时间和近期进食而波动,因此血浆锌正常并不能排除缺锌。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 儿童出现生长迟缓和性成熟延迟,持续性腹泻又反过来加重缺锌形成恶性循环,还有脱发,以及口周、眼周、外阴部和手足部特征性的大疱性结痂皮炎。细胞介导免疫功能受损,表现为胸腺萎缩和T细胞计数下降。在低收入地区的幼儿中,缺锌对腹泻病和肺炎死亡有可测量的促成作用。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 皮炎、味觉障碍、腹泻和免疫功能在补锌后数天至数周内恢复,而且往往恢复明显。线性生长是无法完全追赶的部分:在跨越生长期的长期缺锌中损失的身高只能部分恢复,成年后最终身高可能仍然偏矮。
items.at_risk_zh: 以谷物为主、富含植酸而动物蛋白摄入少的饮食人群,这是全球最主要的膳食模式。低收入地区的儿童。因克罗恩病、乳糜泻或短肠导致吸收不良者;接受过减重手术者。长期饮酒者,会造成尿锌丢失增加。慢性腹泻患者、镰状细胞病患者,以及摄入受限的老年人。同时服用高剂量铁补充剂会竞争同一吸收通路。
items.prevalence_zh: 根据各国食物供应中的锌可获得量估算,全球约17.3%的人口存在锌摄入不足风险(Wessells and Brown, 2012)。在高收入国家健康成人中,临床明显的营养性缺锌并不常见。

items.function_short_zh: 硒构成清除氧化损伤和激活甲状腺激素的酶系统。
items.function_full_zh: 硒以硒代半胱氨酸(selenocysteine)的形式掺入约25种人体硒蛋白中。谷胱甘肽过氧化物酶(GPX1至GPX4)可还原过氧化氢和脂质氢过氧化物,其中GPX4特异性地防止铁死亡相关的膜损伤。硫氧还蛋白还原酶(thioredoxin reductase)维持细胞氧化还原状态并支持DNA合成。碘甲腺原氨酸脱碘酶(iodothyronine deiodinase)将T4转化为活性T3,这将硒的状态与甲状腺功能联系起来。硒蛋白P(selenoprotein P)是血浆中的转运形式,也是评估硒状态的最佳指标。本条目中的剂量至关重要。血浆谷胱甘肽过氧化物酶(GPX3)在每日约55微克摄入时达到平台,这正是每日推荐摄入量(RDA)的依据。硒蛋白P的平台值因基线状态而异,大致在每日50至105微克之间:在硒缺乏的中国受试者中约为每日49微克,而在英国成人中总摄入量约为每日105微克(在约55微克习惯摄入基础上加50微克补充剂)。无论按哪个指标,每日200微克都相当于成人RDA的三到四倍,对于已经硒充足的人不会带来任何进一步的酶活性提升,同时已达到每日400微克可耐受最高摄入量的一半。在Nutritional Prevention of Cancer(营养预防癌症)试验中,平均7.7年每日200微克使2型糖尿病发病率上升(风险比1.55,95%置信区间1.03至2.33),这一效应集中在基线硒水平处于最高三分位的受试者中(风险比2.70)。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 克山病(一种地方性心肌病)。大骨节病(Kashin-Beck disease,一种地方性骨关节病)见于同样的低硒地区,与缺硒相关,但并不能完全用缺硒解释。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 血浆硒和谷胱甘肽过氧化物酶活性下降,但完全没有症状。在地方病流行区,亚临床心电图异常和射血分数下降会先于明显疾病出现,这也是通过筛查发现潜在克山病的方式。流行区之外的散发病例通常表现为不明原因的肌病、肌痛或甲床发白。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 克山病急性发作时表现为心源性休克和心律失常,慢性表现为充血性心肌病,伴心脏扩大及多灶性心肌坏死和纤维化。该病典型地侵袭低土壤硒地区的儿童和育龄期女性,若不治疗可致命。柯萨奇病毒被认为是在硒耗竭宿主中触发急性型的协同因素。大骨节病破坏生长板和关节软骨,导致手指变短、踝、膝、腕、肘关节畸形,并造成永久性活动受限。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 早期克山病对补硒反应良好,若在心肌发生重塑之前发现,心力衰竭可显著改善甚至消退。一旦发展为伴有明确纤维化的扩张型心肌病,心肌损伤就不能完全逆转,预后较差。大骨节病造成的软骨坏死及由此产生的关节畸形是永久性的。在中国地方病流行县实施预防性亚硒酸钠干预可预防新发病例,这是因果关系方向正确的最有力证据。
items.at_risk_zh: 低硒土壤带的居民,主要是中国从东北到西南的对角带地区,以及西伯利亚部分地区。长期未添加硒的肠外营养支持者。严重吸收不良、短肠综合征和囊性纤维化患者。透析患者。对于在北美这种土壤硒含量高的地区摄入混合膳食的人来说,饮食性缺硒不是现实的担忧;仅两颗巴西坚果的硒含量就超过成人RDA。
items.prevalence_zh: 目前尚无确切数据可作为全球性数字。克山病曾在中国一个明确界定的低硒地区呈地方性流行,自20世纪70年代开始补充亚硒酸钠及改变食物供应以来,发病率已降至接近零。在美国,单是食物来源的硒摄入量中位数就已超过RDA,饮食性缺硒基本不存在。

items.function_short_zh: 数百种反应的辅因子;每一分子ATP都要与镁结合才能发挥作用。
items.function_full_zh: ATP的生物活性形式是Mg-ATP,因此镁是每一个激酶反应、每一种ATP酶以及DNA和RNA聚合酶不可或缺的参与者,涉及的酶总数超过300种。镁还是一种生理性钙拮抗剂:静息状态下它阻断NMDA受体通道,并减弱血管平滑肌和心肌中的钙内流,这就是镁耗竭会提高神经肌肉兴奋性和心律失常风险的原因。甲状旁腺激素的分泌及靶器官对其的反应也都需要镁,因此镁耗竭会导致低钙血症,且在补镁之前无法纠正。人体内约60%的镁封存在骨骼中,其余大部分位于细胞内,血清中仅占约1%。因此血清镁并不能很好地反映体内总镁状态,即使在真正镁耗竭的人身上也可能正常。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 症状性低镁血症(ICD-10 E83.4)。没有以人名命名的缺乏病;严重表现为低镁性手足搐搦,伴顽固性低钙血症和低钾血症。遗传性肾性失镁(Gitelman综合征、家族性低镁血症伴高钙尿症)属于遗传性肾小管疾病,不是饮食性缺乏。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 通常完全没有症状。低摄入表现为摄入量低于估计平均需要量,而血清镁正常,因为肾脏会积极地保留镁。患者最先察觉到的是肌肉痉挛、眼睑或手部震颤,以及易激惹或睡眠不佳,这些表现都缺乏特异性。实际中,血清镁偏低最常是在为不明原因低钾血症或低钙血症所做的代谢检查中偶然发现的。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 手足搐搦,Chvostek征和Trousseau征阳性,感觉异常,癫痫发作,以及心律失常,包括心房颤动和尖端扭转型室速。伴随的低钾血症和低钙血症在补镁之前均难以纠正,这是临床上的重要教学要点。严重病例几乎总是由药物或消化道、肾脏丢失所致,而非单纯饮食因素。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 补镁可纠正神经肌肉和心脏方面的表现,并使相关的钾、钙异常随之纠正,一旦基础病因得到处理就不会遗留缺陷。这里需要注意的只是恢复所需的时间:血清镁的恢复正常早于体内总储备的恢复,骨骼和细胞内的镁池需要数天至数周才能补足,过早停止补充会导致缺乏复发。
items.at_risk_zh: 长期饮酒,是主要病因之一。慢性腹泻、吸收不良、短肠综合征及减重手术后引起的消化道丢失,连同肾脏丢失,构成了临床所见低镁血症的很大一部分。长期使用质子泵抑制剂,可引起严重低镁血症。袢利尿剂和噻嗪类利尿剂、顺铂、两性霉素及钙调神经磷酸酶抑制剂;药物性病因在住院人群中占主导。血糖控制不佳伴渗透性利尿的糖尿病患者。再喂养综合征。对于肾脏和肠道功能均正常的人,单纯饮食因素很少导致症状性缺镁。
items.prevalence_zh: 约48%的美国人(各年龄段合计)从食物和饮料中摄入的镁低于其估计平均需要量(NHANES 2013至2016)。具有临床意义的低镁血症并不像这一数字所暗示的那样普遍:一般人群中约为2.5%至15%,住院患者中升至约10%至20%,重症监护患者中更高。摄入不足数字与临床数字之间的差距,正是低摄入常被夸大为普遍缺乏的原因。

items.supplement: Calcium supplements on top of an adequate diet
items.supplement_zh: 钙补充剂(在饮食已充足的基础上额外补充)
items.function_short_zh: 构建骨矿物质,并传递肌肉收缩、神经放电和凝血的信号。
items.function_full_zh: 人体内约99%的钙以羟基磷灰石晶体形式存在于骨骼和牙齿中,发挥结构作用。剩余1%是细胞通用的第二信使:触发肌肉的兴奋收缩偶联、突触处神经递质释放,以及凝血级联反应中的若干步骤。血清游离钙受甲状旁腺激素、骨化三醇和骨吸收的严格调节,维持在很窄的范围内,因此饮食摄入不足不会降低血钙,由骨骼来承担这部分支出。这种调节机制正是本条目的关键所在。随着摄入量增加,吸收分数会下降,因此对于已经从食物中摄入足量钙的人来说,额外补充的钙对骨矿物质的贡献很小,多余部分大多被排出体外。补充剂相较于食物真正带来的额外效应,是一次性大量的吸收负荷,这正是便秘、Women's Health Initiative(妇女健康倡议)研究中观察到的肾结石风险增加,以及尚有争议的心血管信号背后的原因。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 儿童缺钙性佝偻病和成人骨软化症,伴营养性继发性甲状旁腺功能亢进。这是真正低摄入所致的疾病,与饮食已充足者是否额外补充钙剂无关。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 患者不会察觉任何异常。生化层面,甲状旁腺激素升高而血清钙保持正常,尿钙下降,骨转换标志物升高。骨骼正在被悄悄消耗,这就是为何早期阶段只能在因其他原因做检查时被偶然发现。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 儿童出现佝偻病,表现为腿部弯曲、腕部和肋软骨连接处增宽、骨痛和生长迟缓。成人出现骨软化症,表现为弥漫性骨痛、近端肌无力和假性骨折,数十年间骨量加速丢失,脆性骨折风险增加。伴手足搐搦和感觉异常的症状性低钙血症,病因是甲状旁腺或维生素D功能衰竭;单纯饮食摄入不足很少导致这种情况,因为骨骼对摄入不足的缓冲作用非常有效。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 佝偻病和骨软化症在补钙(若同时缺乏维生素D,也需补充维生素D)后可以痊愈,骨矿物质密度大部分可恢复。有两点无法完全恢复:生长期儿童已形成的骨骼畸形及由此损失的身高,以及青春期未能积累的峰值骨量,后者决定了终生基线,日后补充也无法重建。
items.at_risk_zh: 撒哈拉以南非洲和南亚部分地区饮食低钙、高植酸的儿童,当地已记录到的膳食摄入量约为每日200毫克。不摄入乳制品也没有强化替代品的成人。吸收不良、胃切除术后状态、长期使用糖皮质激素,以及未治疗的乳糜泻。本条目所描述的人群,即饮食已满足需求的人,按定义就不属于风险人群,这正是本条目的要点所在。
items.prevalence_zh: 作为钙特异性缺乏的全球数字无确切数据,因为在调查数据中很难将其与维生素D缺乏区分开。区域性数据则有充分记录:患营养性佝偻病的尼日利亚儿童膳食钙摄入量中位数约为每日203毫克,对照组为每日196毫克(P=0.64),而按年龄不同,需求量约为每日700至1,300毫克。在治疗上,单用钙的效果优于单用维生素D:61%接受钙治疗者和58%接受联合治疗者达到复合终点,而仅接受维生素D治疗者为19%。

items.function_short_zh: 并非一种营养素。肠道和口腔中的细菌将其转化为一氧化氮,从而扩张血管。
items.function_full_zh: 来自甜菜根和绿叶蔬菜的无机硝酸盐在近端小肠被吸收,循环池中约四分之一会被唾液腺主动富集。舌背的共生细菌将其还原为亚硝酸盐,吞咽的亚硝酸盐在酸性胃环境及缺氧组织中,经脱氧血红蛋白、脱氧肌红蛋白、黄嘌呤氧化还原酶(xanthine oxidoreductase)及其他金属蛋白进一步还原为一氧化氮。这条肠道唾液循环通路是一条补充性供应线,与人体自身通过一氧化氮合酶(nitric oxide synthase, NOS)以L-精氨酸合成一氧化氮的主要且始终存在的通路并行运作。这一区别使硝酸盐成为可利用的底物,不是人体必需的营养素:即便饮食中不含硝酸盐,NOS来源的一氧化氮合成仍照常进行。已测得的效应是药理性的且呈剂量依赖:血管扩张伴血压轻度下降,以及次极量运动的耗氧量降低。抗菌漱口水通过杀灭还原硝酸盐的口腔菌群而完全消除这一效应,这清楚地表明该机制本质上是微生物性的,不是营养性的。
items.at_risk_zh: 不适用。没有人会缺乏膳食硝酸盐,因为人体对其没有需求,并能独立合成一氧化氮。不吃甜菜根和绿叶蔬菜的人血浆亚硝酸盐水平较低,也就无法获得降压和提高运动经济性的效应,这属于错失了一种药理学益处,不属于缺乏状态。
items.prevalence_zh: 不适用。膳食硝酸盐不是必需营养素,也没有缺乏状态,因此不存在患病率数字,也不应引用任何数字。这里给出的是效应量级的参考,不是缺乏患病率的数字:汇总试验报告收缩压降低约3至5 mmHg,在高血压受试者中降幅最大。

items.function_short: Long-chain fats built into brain, retina and heart cell membranes; they also help resolve inflammation.
items.function_full: EPA (20:5n-3) and DHA (22:6n-3) are the long-chain products of omega-3 metabolism. DHA is the dominant structural fatty acid of retinal photoreceptor outer segments and neuronal synaptic membranes, where it sets membrane fluidity and supports the function of embedded proteins such as rhodopsin. EPA is the substrate for series-3 prostaglandins and series-5 leukotrienes, and both are precursors of the resolvins and protectins that actively terminate inflammation. Because the body can make them from alpha-linolenic acid, they are classed as conditionally essential rather than strictly essential; the conversion is inefficient enough that tissue levels track intake of preformed EPA and DHA closely.
items.deficiency_name: NONE. No named clinical deficiency disease exists for EPA and DHA specifically, because they can be synthesised from ALA.
items.deficiency_early: Nothing a person would notice. The first measurable change is biochemical: a falling omega-3 index, meaning EPA plus DHA as a percentage of red cell fatty acids. Values at or below about 4% define the low band and 8% or above was the proposed target (Harris and von Schacky, PMID 15208005). Symptoms sometimes attributed to low omega-3 status, such as dry skin or low mood, are non-specific and have not been shown to track the index.
items.deficiency_severe: There is no severe clinical syndrome attributable to low EPA and DHA alone in an adult who is otherwise fed. Frank neurological deficiency signs belong to total omega-3 deprivation, which is an ALA problem (see that entry). The clearest documented consequence of low long-chain omega-3 supply is developmental: preterm infants cut off from third-trimester placental DHA transfer accrete far less retinal and brain DHA, with fetal accretion roughly doubling in the last five weeks of gestation.
items.reversibility_note: In adults repletion is complete. Red cell EPA and DHA rise over roughly three to four months, approximately the erythrocyte lifespan, and normalise fully with sustained intake. The partial designation covers the perinatal window only: in rhesus monkeys deprived of n-3 before birth, brain phospholipids had normalised by three years but retinal DHA reached only 84% of controls. Behavioural visual acuity thresholds were normal at 4, 8 and 12 weeks, but cone and rod ERG a-wave amplitudes stayed persistently reduced, so the residue after prenatal deprivation is functional as well as biochemical, and the study answers its own title question in the negative (Anderson GJ et al., Pediatr Res. 2005;58:865-72).
items.at_risk: People who eat no oily fish and take no supplement. Vegans and vegetarians, who have no direct dietary source of preformed EPA or DHA. Preterm infants. Carriers of FADS1/FADS2 minor alleles, who have lower desaturase activity and convert ALA less efficiently.
items.prevalence: Not a disease rate. As a status distribution, omega-3 index values at or below 4% are typical across North America, Central and South America, Europe, the Middle East, Southeast Asia and Africa, while levels above 8% occur mainly around the Sea of Japan, in Scandinavia and in some indigenous coastal populations, based on 298 studies (Stark et al., PMID 27216485).
items.source: PMID 15208005 (Harris WS, von Schacky C. Prev Med. 2004); PMID 27216485 (Stark KD et al. Prog Lipid Res. 2016); Anderson GJ, Neuringer M, Lin DS, Connor WE. Pediatr Res. 2005;58:865-72, doi:10.1203/01.pdr.0000182188.31596.5a
corrections_applied: reversibility_note: added the persistent cone and rod ERG a-wave deficit from Anderson et al., which the original note omitted while keeping the two reassuring findings from the same study; PARTIAL rating left unchanged as the checker directed
source: added the Anderson et al. 2005 citation that the rhesus claims rest on

items.supplement: ALA from flaxseed, chia or walnut oil
items.function_short: The one omega-3 fat the body cannot make; the raw material for EPA and DHA.
items.function_full: Alpha-linolenic acid (18:3n-3) is a genuine essential nutrient. Humans lack the desaturase that places a double bond at the n-3 position of a fatty acid, so every omega-3 molecule in the body traces back to dietary ALA or to preformed EPA and DHA. ALA is incorporated into membrane phospholipids, is a substantial oxidative fuel (a large share of an ingested dose is simply burned), and is the substrate for the elongation and desaturation pathway producing EPA, DPA and DHA. Stable-isotope tracer work puts net conversion to EPA at about 8% in young men and 21% in young women, with DHA formation around 9% in women and undetectable in men (PMID 12323085, PMID 12323090). The US Adequate Intake is 1.6 g/day for men and 1.1 g/day for women.
items.deficiency_name: Alpha-linolenic acid deficiency, the n-3 form of essential fatty acid deficiency (EFAD). It is a recognised clinical entity but carries no eponym comparable to scurvy or rickets.
items.deficiency_early: Biochemically, a rising ratio of n-6 to n-3 fatty acids in plasma and red cell phospholipids with falling 22:6n-3, detectable before any symptom. Clinically, the first reported signs in humans were sensory: intermittent numbness and paraesthesia in the limbs, and blurring of vision.
items.deficiency_severe: In the index case, a six-year-old girl maintained on parenteral nutrition rich in linoleate but nearly devoid of linolenate developed, after five months, episodes of numbness, paraesthesia, leg pain, weakness, inability to walk and blurred vision (Holman et al., PMID 6801965). Patients on long-term gastric-tube feeding with n-3-poor formulas developed scaly dermatitis and a haemorrhagic folliculitis (Bjerve et al.). Deficiency of this severity effectively arises only when the entire fat supply is medically controlled.
items.reversibility_note: In every documented human case, neurological symptoms disappeared and skin lesions resolved once an n-3-containing lipid source was substituted, with plasma fatty acid profiles normalising alongside. No residual deficit was reported. The honest caveat is that all reported cases were identified within months; the consequences of much longer deprivation in humans are unknown.
items.at_risk: Patients on long-term parenteral nutrition or tube feeding with lipid sources low in n-3, historically safflower-based emulsions. Essentially nobody eating ordinary food, since ALA is widespread in vegetable oils, nuts, seeds and green leaves. Extremely low-fat diets sustained for years are a theoretical risk with no case series behind it.
items.prevalence: NOT ESTABLISHED. Clinical ALA deficiency exists only in case reports and small series of parenteral and tube-fed patients. No population prevalence figure exists because the condition does not occur in free-living people eating normal diets.
items.source: PMID 6801965 (Holman RT, Johnson SB, Hatch TF. Am J Clin Nutr. 1982;35:617-23); PMID 12323085 and PMID 12323090 (Burdge GC et al. Br J Nutr. 2002); Institute of Medicine DRI for Macronutrients 2005, doi:10.17226/10490
corrections_applied: none: no defect raised against this entry, and the checker verified the CLINICAL classification, the FULL reversibility call and the Burdge conversion figures; left verbatim

items.function_short: Oil from marine microalgae that supplies ready-made DHA, and in some products EPA, without fish.
items.function_full: Algal oil is extracted from cultured heterotrophic microalgae, chiefly Schizochytrium species and Crypthecodinium cohnii. These are the organisms at the base of the marine food chain that actually synthesise DHA; fish accumulate it by eating them. Crypthecodinium products supply DHA only, while Schizochytrium products supply DHA plus a smaller amount of EPA. Physiologically the oil does nothing that DHA and EPA do not do, so the mechanism sits in the Omega-3 (EPA and DHA) entry. Controlled feeding work found algal-oil capsules and cooked salmon to be nutritionally equivalent sources of DHA in terms of plasma incorporation (PMID 18589030), which is why algal DHA has been the standard source in infant formula for decades.
items.deficiency_early: NOT APPLICABLE. Algal oil is a manufactured delivery form, not a nutrient, and nobody becomes deficient in it. The status question that matters is DHA and EPA status, answered in the Omega-3 (EPA and DHA) entry.
items.reversibility_note: NOT APPLICABLE. There is no algal oil deficiency to reverse.
items.at_risk: NOT APPLICABLE as a deficiency. As a practical supply point, algal oil is the only direct dietary source of preformed DHA for people who eat no fish, since ALA conversion yields little DHA in women and none detectable in men.
items.source: PMID 18589030 (Arterburn LM et al. J Am Diet Assoc. 2008;108:1204-9)
corrections_applied: deficiency_state: NA changed to NONE. The question was evaluated and the answer is that no deficiency state exists for a manufactured product made from a living organism; NA is reserved for a compound product whose constituent nutrients each have their own entry, which this is not (its single nutrient pair has one entry)
reversibility_note: kept NA and added the reason, so the field reads as a deficiency answer rather than a blank

items.function_short: Oil from Antarctic krill delivering EPA and DHA largely bound to phospholipids, plus some astaxanthin.
items.function_full: Krill oil is extracted from Euphausia superba. Its distinguishing feature is chemical form: a large share of the EPA and DHA is esterified to phospholipid, mainly phosphatidylcholine, with some present as free fatty acid, whereas fish oil carries them as triglycerides or ethyl esters. This alters absorption kinetics. It also contains small amounts of astaxanthin, a carotenoid acting as an antioxidant within the oil. EPA plus DHA content per capsule is typically lower than in fish oil, so dose comparisons need to be made per milligram of omega-3. Acute crossover studies find equal or modestly higher plasma phospholipid incorporation from krill per unit EPA plus DHA (PMID 21854650), but a reanalysis of these studies concluded the acute differences have not translated reliably into different long-term omega-3 status (PMID 25156381).
items.deficiency_early: NOT APPLICABLE. Krill oil is a manufactured product category, not an essential nutrient, and no deficiency state exists for it. The relevant physiology is EPA and DHA status, covered in the Omega-3 (EPA and DHA) entry.
items.reversibility_note: NOT APPLICABLE. There is no krill oil deficiency to reverse.
items.source: PMID 21854650 (Schuchardt JP et al. Lipids Health Dis. 2011); PMID 25156381 (Salem N Jr, Kuratko CN. Lipids Health Dis. 2014)
corrections_applied: deficiency_state: NA changed to NONE. The entry's own text calls krill oil a commercial product category for which no deficiency state exists, which is the NONE answer; NA is reserved for compound products whose constituent nutrients are covered by separate entries
reversibility_note: kept NA and added the reason, matching the other evaluated-and-none rows

items.function_short: Concentrated food protein supplying the amino acids used to build and repair muscle and every tissue.
items.function_full: Protein powder is isolated food protein (whey, casein, soy, pea, rice, egg) dried and concentrated. It has no function of its own; the function is that of dietary protein, which supplies the nine indispensable amino acids plus nitrogen for synthesis of muscle, enzymes, albumin, immunoglobulins, haemoglobin, hormones and connective tissue. An adult turns over roughly 250 to 300 g of body protein daily, most of it recycled, with dietary intake covering obligatory oxidative losses. The US RDA is 0.8 g/kg/day. The PROT-AGE group recommends 1.0 to 1.2 g/kg/day for healthy older adults and 1.2 to 1.5 g/kg/day in acute or chronic illness, because the muscle protein synthetic response to a given protein dose is blunted with age (PMID 23867520).
items.deficiency_name: Protein-energy malnutrition, presenting as marasmus and as wasting. Two conditions often listed here do not belong to dietary protein. Kwashiorkor is a form of severe acute malnutrition of uncertain aetiology, not the consequence of eating too little protein: affected children often have protein intakes comparable to marasmic children, some are still breastfed, and high-protein repletion does not preferentially resolve it. Sarcopenia is a muscle disease of ageing, inactivity, inflammation, anabolic resistance and comorbidity under the EWGSOP2 definition, and it occurs in older adults meeting the RDA; low protein intake is one modifiable contributor to it, not the deficiency state itself.
items.deficiency_early: Unintentional weight loss, falling mid-upper arm circumference, loss of subcutaneous fat and muscle bulk, thinning brittle hair, delayed wound healing and more frequent infections. Serum albumin falls late and is heavily confounded by inflammation, so it is a poor early marker. In older adults, declining grip strength and slower gait speed usually appear before visible muscle loss.
items.deficiency_severe: Marasmus is severe wasting: weight-for-height far below normal, visible loss of muscle and fat, an aged appearance in a young child. Kwashiorkor adds pitting oedema, an enlarged fatty liver, flaky-paint skin desquamation and hair depigmentation. Both carry high case fatality from hypoglycaemia, hypothermia, electrolyte disturbance and overwhelming infection; without structured refeeding the endpoint is death. In older adults, untreated sarcopenia ends in falls, fracture, loss of independence and raised mortality.
items.reversibility_note: Acute wasting reverses with careful staged refeeding, and weight-for-height recovers. What does not fully recover is linear growth and neurocognitive development when the episode falls within the first 1000 days: stunting established before age two is largely permanent, and the associated cognitive deficits persist into adulthood. Sarcopenia is partly reversible, since resistance training with adequate protein rebuilds strength and some mass, but muscle lost over decades is not fully regained.
items.at_risk: Children in food-insecure settings, especially around weaning and following infection. Hospitalised, post-surgical and critically ill patients. Older adults with poor appetite, dental problems, dysphagia or social isolation. People with malabsorption, cirrhosis, or cachexia from cancer, advanced kidney or heart failure. Anorexia nervosa. Healthy adults in wealthy countries eating adequate calories almost never fall short of protein.
items.prevalence: In 2024, 42.8 million children under five were wasted (6.6%) and 12.2 million severely wasted (1.9%); 150.2 million were stunted (UNICEF/WHO/World Bank Joint Malnutrition Estimates, 2025 edition). Pooled sarcopenia prevalence in older adults is 17.7% under EWGSOP1 and 11% under EWGSOP2, with study-level ranges of 6.2% to 35.3% and 3.2% to 26.3% respectively (Fernandes LV et al., Aging Clin Exp Res. 2022;34:505-514).
items.source: UNICEF/WHO/World Bank Joint Child Malnutrition Estimates 2025 (https://data.unicef.org/resources/jme/); PMID 23867520 (Bauer J et al. PROT-AGE. J Am Med Dir Assoc. 2013;14:542-59); doi:10.1007/s40520-021-01951-7 (Fernandes LV et al. Aging Clin Exp Res. 2022;34:505-514, sarcopenia prevalence under EWGSOP1 and EWGSOP2)
corrections_applied: prevalence: replaced the 10-27% range and the claim that EWGSOP2 sits at its lower end with the figures the cited paper actually reports, 17.7% (EWGSOP1) and 11% (EWGSOP2) with ranges 6.2-35.3% and 3.2-26.3%, keeping the existing citation as the checker permitted

deficiency_name: removed kwashiorkor as a protein deficiency state and restated it as a form of severe acute malnutrition of uncertain aetiology, with the reasons (comparable protein intakes to marasmic children, some still breastfed, no preferential response to high-protein repletion)

items.function_short: An amino acid the body makes itself; a preferred fuel for gut lining and immune cells.
items.function_full: Glutamine is the most abundant free amino acid in plasma and skeletal muscle. Muscle synthesises and exports it continuously via glutamine synthetase, so supply is normally set by endogenous production rather than by diet. Enterocytes and rapidly dividing immune cells use it as a preferred respiratory fuel and as the nitrogen donor for purine, pyrimidine and glutathione synthesis, which is the biochemistry behind the gut-repair claim. It is classed as non-essential in health and conditionally essential in severe catabolic states, where muscle export cannot keep pace with consumption. Human trials of oral glutamine for intestinal permeability, IBS and inflammatory bowel disease have been small and inconsistent, and the strongest evidence is in specific clinical contexts rather than in healthy people.
items.deficiency_early: NOT APPLICABLE. There is no dietary requirement for glutamine and therefore no dietary deficiency to detect. Low plasma glutamine arises as a consequence of critical illness, major trauma or burns, not of what someone eats.
items.deficiency_severe: NOT APPLICABLE. Plasma glutamine below 0.420 mmol/L on ICU admission was associated with higher mortality in 80 non-elective admissions (Oudemans-van Straaten HM et al., PMID 11280678), but it marks the severity of catabolism rather than a nutrient shortfall. Treating it as a deficiency to correct proved harmful: in the REDOXS trial of 1223 ventilated ICU patients with multi-organ failure, high-dose glutamine increased in-hospital and six-month mortality (PMID 23594003).
items.reversibility_note: NOT APPLICABLE. There is no glutamine deficiency to reverse.
items.at_risk: NOT APPLICABLE. Nobody becomes glutamine-deficient from diet. Low plasma concentrations occur in sepsis, major burns, major trauma and prolonged critical illness, and reflect the underlying illness.
items.source: PMID 11280678 (Oudemans-van Straaten HM et al. Intensive Care Med. 2001;27:84-90); PMID 23594003 (Heyland D et al. N Engl J Med. 2013;368:1489-97)
corrections_applied: deficiency_severe: attached the 0.420 mmol/L threshold to its actual source (PMID 11280678, 80 non-elective ICU admissions) instead of leaving it uncited under REDOXS, which does not report that cut-off; REDOXS description left as written since the checker verified it
source: added PMID 11280678
reversibility_note: kept NA and stated the reason

items.function_short: Hydrolysed animal collagen eaten as protein; the body builds its own collagen from ordinary amino acids.
items.function_full: Collagen is the most abundant protein in the body, roughly a third of total body protein, forming the tensile framework of skin, tendon, ligament, bone matrix, cartilage and vessel wall. The body synthesises it from ordinary amino acids as a repeating Gly-X-Y sequence rich in proline; the post-translational hydroxylation that stabilises the triple helix is carried out by prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases, which require vitamin C, iron and 2-oxoglutarate. Ingested collagen is digested like any other protein, though some di- and tripeptides such as prolyl-hydroxyproline do reach the bloodstream intact, which is the proposed mechanism for any effect beyond amino acid supply. As a protein source collagen is nutritionally incomplete: it contains no tryptophan and is low in several other indispensable amino acids.
items.deficiency_name: NONE. Scurvy is sometimes described loosely as a collagen deficiency, which is a misreading: it is vitamin C deficiency, and the defective collagen is downstream of the missing enzyme cofactor.
items.deficiency_early: NOT APPLICABLE. Collagen is not a dietary requirement and there is no dietary collagen deficiency. Real failures of collagen come from vitamin C deficiency (scurvy), from inherited defects in collagen genes (osteogenesis imperfecta, the Ehlers-Danlos syndromes), or from overall protein-energy malnutrition. None of these is corrected by eating collagen.
items.reversibility_note: NOT APPLICABLE. There is no dietary collagen deficiency to reverse.
items.at_risk: NOT APPLICABLE. One theoretical argument deserves mention without overstatement: a stoichiometric analysis calculated that endogenous glycine synthesis plus typical dietary glycine falls roughly 10 g/day short of the amount required for maximal collagen turnover in a 70 kg adult (PMID 20093739). This remains a calculation. No glycine or collagen deficiency state has been demonstrated clinically.
items.source: PMID 20093739 (Melendez-Hevia E et al. J Biosci. 2009;34:853-72); NCBI Bookshelf NBK507709 (Biochemistry, Collagen Synthesis, StatPearls)
corrections_applied: none on substance: no defect raised, and the checker singled this entry out for correctly separating dietary collagen from vitamin C deficiency and from the genetic collagen disorders; kept the genetic conditions in prose and out of the deficiency slot
reversibility_note: kept NA and stated the reason, no change of meaning

items.function_short: A gel-forming fibre that holds water in stool, making it softer, bulkier and easier to pass.
items.function_full: Psyllium is the milled seed husk of Plantago ovata, largely a highly branched arabinoxylan that is gel-forming and, unusually among viscous fibres, poorly fermented by colonic bacteria. Because it survives intact to the rectum it retains its water there, producing bulky soft stool with far less gas than fermentable fibres. It normalises stool form in both directions, softening hard stool and firming loose stool. The same gel raises the viscosity of small intestinal contents, which slows glucose absorption and traps bile acids; the resulting loss of bile acids drives hepatic synthesis from cholesterol and lowers LDL. In IBS it is the fibre with actual trial support: ispaghula gave a relative risk of IBS not improving of 0.83 (95% CI 0.73 to 0.94), number needed to treat 7 (95% CI 4 to 25), and is the fibre recommended by the ACG guideline (PMID 33315591).
items.deficiency_early: NOT APPLICABLE. There is no psyllium deficiency; psyllium is one way to correct a shortfall in total dietary fibre, and that shortfall belongs to total fibre, which has no entry of its own in this group. Low fibre intake shows up first as harder and less frequent stools, straining, longer whole-gut transit time and reduced stool weight.
items.deficiency_severe: NOT APPLICABLE. No deficiency disease follows from low fibre intake either. What the evidence supports is a graded association: pooling 185 prospective studies and 58 trials, the highest fibre intake groups had 15% to 30% lower all-cause and cardiovascular mortality than the lowest, with lower incidence of coronary heart disease, stroke, type 2 diabetes and colorectal cancer. The greatest risk reduction fell between 25 and 29 g/day, with dose-response curves suggesting, but not demonstrating, further benefit above 30 g/day (Reynolds et al., PMID 30638909). Untreated chronic constipation can itself progress to faecal impaction and, rarely, stercoral ulceration or perforation.
items.reversibility_note: NOT APPLICABLE. There is no psyllium deficiency to reverse. The effects of taking it are pharmacodynamic: stool form, frequency, transit time and the LDL and post-prandial glucose changes correct within days to a few weeks of adequate intake and revert when intake stops. The mortality and cancer associations relate to long-term dietary pattern rather than to short-term supplementation, and no trial has shown a fibre supplement reverses established colorectal neoplasia.
items.at_risk: NOT APPLICABLE as a deficiency. For low total fibre intake: most people eating a Western diet, particularly those eating mainly refined grains with few vegetables, pulses or fruit, and anyone on a prolonged low-residue or restrictive diet. Mean US adult intake is about 16 g/day against an Adequate Intake of 25 g/day for younger women and 38 g/day for younger men.
items.prevalence: NOT APPLICABLE. No requirement exists for psyllium, so no adequacy figure exists for it. For total dietary fibre, roughly 5% of the US population meets the Adequate Intake (Quagliani D, Felt-Gunderson P. Am J Lifestyle Med. 2017;11:80-85) and 7.4% of US adults meet 14 g per 1000 kcal (Miketinas DC et al., usual fibre intake, NHANES 2013-2018); mean US adult intake is about 16 g/day (WWEIA NHANES 2009-2010, NCBI Bookshelf NBK589559).
items.source: PMID 30638909 (Reynolds A et al. Lancet. 2019;393:434-45); PMID 33315591 (Lacy BE et al. ACG Clinical Guideline: Management of IBS. Am J Gastroenterol. 2021;116:17-44); Quagliani D, Felt-Gunderson P. Am J Lifestyle Med. 2017;11:80-85 (5% meeting the fibre AI); Miketinas DC et al., NHANES 2013-2018 (7.4% meeting 14 g/1000 kcal); NCBI Bookshelf NBK589559, FSRG Dietary Data Brief, WWEIA NHANES 2009-2010 (mean 16 g/day)
corrections_applied: deficiency_state: FUNCTIONAL changed to NONE, per the misclassification finding. A FUNCTIONAL state paired with a NONE deficiency name is not allowed, and the shortfall being described belongs to total dietary fibre, not to psyllium
deficiency_early, deficiency_severe, at_risk, prevalence: prefixed NOT APPLICABLE to match the NONE state, with the substantive fibre evidence kept as prose rather than deleted

reversibility: FULL changed to NA, since there is no deficiency to recover from; the days-to-weeks response and its reversal on stopping were restated in the note as pharmacodynamics of taking the product

deficiency_severe: 'Benefit accrued across 25 to 29 g/day with more above 30 g/day' softened to what Reynolds et al. actually claimed, greatest risk reduction at 25-29 g/day with dose-response curves suggesting but not demonstrating further benefit above 30 g/day; the 185 studies, 58 trials and 15-30% figures were verified and left alone

prevalence and source: moved the 5% and 7.4% figures off NBK589559, which does not report either, onto Quagliani and Felt-Gunderson and Miketinas et al. respectively; NBK589559 retained only for the 16 g/day mean it does support

items.function_short: Fibres your gut bacteria feed on, boosting bifidobacteria and producing short-chain fatty acids in the colon.
items.function_full: Inulin and fructo-oligosaccharides are fructose polymers from chicory root, Jerusalem artichoke, onion, garlic and wheat, differing mainly in chain length: FOS has a degree of polymerisation below about 9, inulin extends to 60. GOS are galactose oligomers produced enzymatically from lactose and are structural analogues of human milk oligosaccharides. All three resist human digestive enzymes, reach the colon intact and are selectively fermented, reproducibly raising Bifidobacterium abundance, which is the basis of the ISAPP definition of a prebiotic as a substrate selectively used by host microorganisms to confer a health benefit (PMID 28611480). Fermentation yields acetate, propionate and butyrate; butyrate is the primary respiratory fuel of the colonocyte, and the short-chain fatty acid pool lowers luminal pH and supports barrier function. That same fermentability produces the gas and bloating these compounds are known for, and is why they are classed as high-FODMAP.
items.deficiency_early: NOT APPLICABLE. No prebiotic-specific deficiency exists and no requirement has been set. Low intake of fermentable substrate lowers colonic short-chain fatty acid production, particularly butyrate, and reduces Bifidobacterium abundance. Both are measurable in stool, neither produces a symptom a person would notice, and both are pharmacodynamic responses to an intake rather than a deficiency state.
items.deficiency_severe: NOT APPLICABLE. There is no severe deficiency syndrome in humans. The strongest mechanistic finding comes from mice: under chronic or intermittent fibre deprivation the microbiota switches to degrading host-secreted mucus glycoproteins, thinning the colonic mucus barrier and increasing susceptibility to an enteric pathogen (Desai et al., PMID 27863247). This has not been shown to produce disease in people, and the human outcomes attributed to low fibre intake are best assessed at the level of total fibre rather than prebiotics specifically.
items.reversibility_note: NOT APPLICABLE. There is no prebiotic deficiency to reverse. The response to taking one is pharmacodynamic: Bifidobacterium abundance and short-chain fatty acid output rise within days to about a week of intake and return toward baseline over a similar period after stopping. The effect is intake-dependent throughout, and no durable change in microbiota composition persists once supplementation ends.
items.at_risk: NOT APPLICABLE as a deficiency. As a supply point, low intake occurs in anyone eating little onion, garlic, leek, chicory, wheat, banana or legume. People following a low-FODMAP diet for IBS restrict precisely these substrates and show measurable falls in Bifidobacterium, which is why the restriction phase is intended to be time-limited and followed by structured reintroduction. Infants on formulas without added GOS or FOS receive none.
items.prevalence: NOT APPLICABLE. No requirement has been set for prebiotics, so no adequacy figure exists. Habitual inulin-type fructan intake in Europe and the US is estimated at roughly 1 to 10 g/day.
items.source: PMID 28611480 (Gibson GR et al. ISAPP consensus statement on prebiotics. Nat Rev Gastroenterol Hepatol. 2017;14:491-502); PMID 27863247 (Desai MS et al. Cell. 2016;167:1339-53)
corrections_applied: deficiency_state: FUNCTIONAL changed to NONE, per the misclassification finding. The entry contradicted its own label three times, no requirement exists, and the only severe-consequence evidence is a mouse experiment the entry itself flags as unshown in people
deficiency_early, deficiency_severe, at_risk, prevalence: prefixed NOT APPLICABLE to match the NONE state; prevalence changed from NOT ESTABLISHED to NOT APPLICABLE for the same reason
reversibility: FULL changed to NA; the days-to-a-week bifidobacteria and SCFA response was restated in the note as a pharmacodynamic response to intake, not recovery from a deficiency
deficiency_early: named the bifidobacteria and butyrate changes as pharmacodynamic responses rather than deficiency markers, as the checker required

items.supplement: Wheat bran and insoluble fibre supplements for IBS
items.function_short: Coarse insoluble fibre that adds stool bulk mechanically; in IBS it often makes symptoms worse.
items.function_full: Wheat bran is the outer layer of the wheat kernel, composed mainly of insoluble arabinoxylan, cellulose and lignin. It acts through particle bulk and mechanical stimulation of the mucosa rather than by forming a gel: coarse particles increase stool mass and provoke secretion and peristalsis, whereas finely ground bran loses this effect and can slow transit. It holds far less water than psyllium and is partly fermented, generating gas. In IBS these properties work against the patient, since mechanical stimulation acts on a hypersensitive gut and bran also carries fructans, making it high-FODMAP. Meta-analysis found no significant benefit of bran for global IBS symptoms (relative risk of not improving 0.90, 95% CI 0.79 to 1.03), in contrast to ispaghula (NNT 7), and the ACG guideline recommends soluble fibre for IBS (PMID 33315591).
items.deficiency_early: NOT APPLICABLE. There is no wheat bran deficiency. Bran is a food fraction sold as a supplement, not a nutrient, and the shortfall worth describing belongs to total dietary fibre, where low intake produces harder and less frequent stools, straining, reduced stool weight and slower whole-gut transit. Withdrawing bran from someone for whom it was the only fibre source reproduces these effects.
items.deficiency_severe: NOT APPLICABLE. Nothing severe follows from not taking a bran supplement. The general low-fibre associations apply: 15% to 30% lower all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in the highest versus lowest total fibre intake groups, with lower coronary heart disease, stroke, type 2 diabetes and colorectal cancer incidence (PMID 30638909). In IBS specifically the more common clinical problem runs the other way. Among 100 consecutive IBS referrals who had tried bran, 55% reported it made them worse and only 10% found it helpful, with bowel disturbance, distension and pain all exacerbated (Francis and Whorwell, PMID 7912305).
items.reversibility_note: NOT APPLICABLE. There is no bran deficiency to reverse. Changes from taking or stopping it are pharmacodynamic: stool bulk, frequency and transit time respond within days of changing insoluble fibre intake and revert on withdrawal, and bran-induced symptom flares in IBS settle once bran is stopped, with no lasting mucosal or functional damage described.
items.at_risk: NOT APPLICABLE as a deficiency. For low total fibre intake: people eating predominantly refined grains with few plant foods, with mean US adult intake around 16 g/day against an Adequate Intake of 25 to 38 g/day. For harm rather than shortfall: people with IBS, who are the population most likely to be given bran and most likely to be worsened by it.
items.prevalence: NOT APPLICABLE. Bran has no requirement and therefore no adequacy figure. For total dietary fibre, about 5% of the US population meets the Adequate Intake (Quagliani D, Felt-Gunderson P. Am J Lifestyle Med. 2017;11:80-85), with mean US adult intake around 16 g/day (WWEIA NHANES 2009-2010, NCBI Bookshelf NBK589559). For bran intolerance in IBS, 55% of 100 consecutive IBS referrals reported symptom worsening on bran (PMID 7912305).
items.source: PMID 7912305 (Francis CY, Whorwell PJ. Lancet. 1994;344:39-40); PMID 30638909 (Reynolds A et al. Lancet. 2019;393:434-45); PMID 33315591 (Lacy BE et al. Am J Gastroenterol. 2021;116:17-44); Quagliani D, Felt-Gunderson P. Am J Lifestyle Med. 2017;11:80-85 (5% meeting the fibre AI); NCBI Bookshelf NBK589559, FSRG Dietary Data Brief, WWEIA NHANES 2009-2010 (mean 16 g/day)
corrections_applied: deficiency_state: FUNCTIONAL changed to NONE, per the misclassification finding. The entry already said there is no wheat bran deficiency and that the functional label belongs to total dietary fibre; FUNCTIONAL implied a shortfall worth correcting with a product whose own cited evidence shows net harm in the named population
deficiency_early, deficiency_severe, at_risk, prevalence: prefixed NOT APPLICABLE to match the NONE state, with the fibre association data and the bran-harm data kept as prose
reversibility: FULL changed to NA; the stool and symptom changes were restated in the note as pharmacodynamic effects of starting or stopping bran, not recovery from a deficiency

prevalence and source: attributed the 5% figure to Quagliani and Felt-Gunderson and the 16 g/day mean to NBK589559 instead of a bare 'NHANES', closing the same citation gap the checker identified in the psyllium entry

items.function_short_zh: 构建脑、视网膜和心脏细胞膜的长链脂肪酸,同时有助于消退炎症。
items.function_full_zh: EPA(20:5n-3)和DHA(22:6n-3)是omega-3代谢的长链产物。DHA是视网膜光感受器外节和神经元突触膜的主要结构脂肪酸,决定膜的流动性,并支持视紫红质等嵌膜蛋白的功能。EPA是3系前列腺素和5系白三烯的底物,两者都是消退素和保护素的前体,这些物质能主动终止炎症。由于人体可以由α-亚麻酸合成EPA和DHA,它们被归为条件必需脂肪酸而非严格必需脂肪酸,但转化效率低,以至于组织中的水平仍紧密跟随预成EPA和DHA的摄入量。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 无。EPA和DHA本身没有专属的临床缺乏病命名,因为它们可以由ALA合成。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 本人不会察觉到任何症状。最早可测得的变化是生化指标:omega-3指数下降,即EPA加DHA占红细胞脂肪酸的百分比。约4%及以下为低水平区间,8%及以上是提出的目标值(Harris和von Schacky,PMID 15208005)。有时被归因于omega-3水平偏低的症状,如皮肤干燥或情绪低落,均属非特异性表现,尚未证实与该指数相关。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 对于饮食其他方面正常的成年人,单纯EPA和DHA偏低不会引起严重临床综合征。明显的神经系统缺乏体征属于omega-3完全缺乏的情形,那是ALA的问题(见该词条)。长链omega-3供应不足最明确记录的后果与发育有关:早产儿因失去妊娠晚期胎盘DHA转运而在视网膜和脑内蓄积的DHA大幅减少,胎儿DHA蓄积速度在妊娠最后五周约翻倍。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 成年人补充后可完全恢复。红细胞EPA和DHA在大约三到四个月内(约相当于红细胞寿命)上升,持续摄入后可完全恢复正常。部分可逆的判定仅针对围产期这一窗口:在出生前被剥夺n-3的恒河猴中,脑磷脂在三岁时已恢复正常,但视网膜DHA仅达到对照组的84%。行为学视敏度阈值在4周、8周和12周时均正常,但视锥和视杆细胞ERG a波振幅持续偏低,因此产前剥夺后留下的残余损害既是功能性的也是生化性的,该研究对自己标题所提的问题给出了否定的答案(Anderson GJ等,Pediatr Res. 2005;58:865-72)。
items.at_risk_zh: 不吃富脂鱼类又不服用补充剂的人。纯素食者和素食者,因为他们没有直接摄入预成EPA或DHA的膳食来源。早产儿。携带FADS1/FADS2次要等位基因的人,其desaturase活性较低,ALA转化效率较差。
items.prevalence_zh: 并非疾病发生率。作为一种状态分布,omega-3指数在4%及以下在北美、中南美洲、欧洲、中东、东南亚和非洲较为常见,而8%以上的水平主要见于日本海周边、斯堪的纳维亚地区以及部分沿海原住民人群,数据基于298项研究(Stark等,PMID 27216485)。

items.supplement: ALA from flaxseed, chia or walnut oil
items.supplement_zh: 亚麻籽、奇亚籽或核桃油中的ALA(α-亚麻酸)
items.function_short_zh: 人体唯一无法自行合成的omega-3脂肪,是EPA和DHA的原料。
items.function_full_zh: α-亚麻酸(18:3n-3)是真正意义上的必需营养素。人体缺乏能在脂肪酸n-3位置引入双键的desaturase,因此体内每一个omega-3分子都来自膳食ALA或预成的EPA和DHA。ALA被掺入膜磷脂,也是重要的氧化燃料(摄入剂量中相当大一部分直接被氧化供能),同时是生成EPA、DPA和DHA的延长去饱和途径的底物。稳定同位素示踪研究显示,年轻男性向EPA的净转化率约为8%,年轻女性约为21%,DHA生成率女性约为9%,男性检测不到(PMID 12323085, PMID 12323090)。美国的适宜摄入量男性为1.6 g/day,女性为1.1 g/day。
items.deficiency_name_zh: α-亚麻酸缺乏症,即必需脂肪酸缺乏症(EFAD)的n-3形式。这是公认的临床实体,但没有类似坏血病或佝偻病那样的专有病名。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 生化上表现为血浆和红细胞磷脂中n-6与n-3脂肪酸比值升高,22:6n-3下降,这在出现任何症状之前即可检测到。临床上,人体首次报告的体征属于感觉方面:间歇性肢体麻木和感觉异常,以及视物模糊。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 在首例报告中,一名6岁女孩接受富含亚油酸盐但几乎不含亚麻酸盐的肠外营养,五个月后出现发作性麻木、感觉异常、腿痛、乏力、无法行走及视物模糊(Holman等,PMID 6801965)。长期使用贫n-3配方经胃管喂养的患者出现鳞屑性皮炎和出血性毛囊炎(Bjerve等)。这种严重程度的缺乏实际上只发生在全部脂肪供给都由医疗手段控制的情况下。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 在所有已记录的人体病例中,一旦改用含n-3的脂质来源,神经系统症状即消失,皮肤病变随之消退,血浆脂肪酸谱同步恢复正常,未见报告有残留缺陷。需要如实说明的是,所有报告病例均在数月内被发现,人体长期缺乏的后果尚不清楚。
items.at_risk_zh: 长期接受肠外营养或管饲、且脂质来源n-3含量低(历史上多为红花籽油基乳剂)的患者。正常饮食的人群基本不会出现风险,因为ALA广泛存在于植物油、坚果、种子和绿叶蔬菜中。持续多年的极低脂饮食是一种理论上的风险,尚无病例系列支持。
items.prevalence_zh: 无确切数据。临床ALA缺乏症仅见于肠外营养和管饲患者的病例报告及小样本系列。由于该病不会发生在正常饮食的普通人群中,没有人群患病率数据。

items.function_short_zh: 来自海洋微藻的油脂,可在不吃鱼的情况下提供现成的DHA,部分产品还含EPA。
items.function_full_zh: 藻油提取自培养的异养微藻,主要是裂殖壶菌属(Schizochytrium)物种和寇氏隐甲藻(Crypthecodinium cohnii)。这些是海洋食物链底端真正合成DHA的生物,鱼类是通过摄食它们而积累DHA。寇氏隐甲藻产品只提供DHA,裂殖壶菌产品则提供DHA外加少量EPA。从生理学角度看,该油脂的作用不超出DHA和EPA本身的作用范围,其机制见Omega-3(EPA和DHA)词条。对照喂养研究发现,就血浆掺入而言,藻油胶囊和熟三文鱼是营养上等效的DHA来源(PMID 18589030),这也是藻源DHA数十年来一直是婴儿配方奶粉标准来源的原因。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 不适用。藻油是一种人工制造的输送形式,不是营养素,没有人会缺乏它。真正重要的状态问题是DHA和EPA水平,答案见Omega-3(EPA和DHA)词条。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 不适用。不存在需要逆转的藻油缺乏。
items.at_risk_zh: 作为缺乏症不适用。从实际供给角度看,对不吃鱼的人来说,藻油是预成DHA唯一的直接膳食来源,因为ALA转化生成的DHA在女性中很少,在男性中检测不到。

items.function_short_zh: 来自南极磷虾的油脂,其中EPA和DHA大多以磷脂形式结合,还含有少量虾青素。
items.function_full_zh: 磷虾油提取自南极磷虾(Euphausia superba)。其显著特点在于化学形式:相当一部分EPA和DHA以磷脂形式酯化,主要是磷脂酰胆碱,部分以游离脂肪酸形式存在,而鱼油中这些成分则以甘油三酯或乙酯形式存在。这会改变吸收动力学。磷虾油还含有少量虾青素,一种在油脂中起抗氧化作用的类胡萝卜素。每粒胶囊所含的EPA加DHA通常低于鱼油,因此剂量比较需按每毫克omega-3计算。急性交叉研究发现,按每单位EPA加DHA计算,磷虾来源的血浆磷脂掺入量相等或略高(PMID 21854650),但一项对这些研究的再分析认为,这种急性差异并未可靠地转化为长期omega-3水平的差异(PMID 25156381)。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 不适用。磷虾油是一种人工制造的产品类别,不是必需营养素,不存在与之对应的缺乏状态。相关生理学问题是EPA和DHA水平,见Omega-3(EPA和DHA)词条。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 不适用。不存在需要逆转的磷虾油缺乏。

items.function_short_zh: 浓缩食物蛋白质,提供用于构建和修复肌肉及各种组织的氨基酸。
items.function_full_zh: 蛋白粉是从食物中分离出的蛋白质(乳清、酪蛋白、大豆、豌豆、大米、鸡蛋),经干燥浓缩而成。它本身没有独立的功能,其作用就是膳食蛋白质的作用:提供9种必需氨基酸以及用于合成肌肉、酶、白蛋白、免疫球蛋白、血红蛋白、激素和结缔组织的氮源。成人每天约有250至300 g体蛋白发生周转,其中大部分被循环利用,膳食摄入用于弥补必然存在的氧化性丢失。美国的推荐膳食摄入量(RDA)为0.8 g/kg/day。PROT-AGE专家组建议健康老年人摄入1.0至1.2 g/kg/day,急性或慢性疾病状态下摄入1.2至1.5 g/kg/day,因为随着年龄增长,给定蛋白剂量引发的肌肉蛋白合成反应会减弱(PMID 23867520)。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 蛋白质能量营养不良,表现为消瘦型营养不良(marasmus)和消瘦。这里常被列入的另外两种情况实际上不属于膳食蛋白质问题。夸希奥科病(kwashiorkor)是一种病因尚不明确的重度急性营养不良,并非蛋白质摄入过少的后果:患病儿童的蛋白质摄入量往往与消瘦型营养不良儿童相当,部分患儿仍在母乳喂养,高蛋白补充也不能优先改善该病。肌少症(sarcopenia)按照EWGSOP2定义是一种由衰老、活动不足、炎症、合成代谢抵抗及合并症共同导致的肌肉疾病,即使摄入量达到RDA的老年人也会发病,蛋白质摄入不足只是其中一个可调节的促成因素,而不是缺乏状态本身。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 非自主性体重下降,上臂中段周径减小,皮下脂肪和肌肉量减少,头发变细变脆,伤口愈合延迟,感染更为频繁。血清白蛋白下降出现较晚,且受炎症严重干扰,因此不是良好的早期指标。老年人中,握力下降和步速减慢通常出现在肉眼可见的肌肉丢失之前。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 消瘦型营养不良表现为严重消瘦:身高别体重远低于正常,肌肉和脂肪明显丢失,幼儿呈现衰老外貌。夸希奥科病在此基础上还有凹陷性水肿、脂肪肝肿大、剥落样皮肤脱屑和毛发脱色。两者都因低血糖、低体温、电解质紊乱和严重感染而具有很高的病死率,若不进行规范化再喂养,结局即为死亡。老年人未经治疗的肌少症最终导致跌倒、骨折、丧失自理能力和死亡率升高。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 急性消瘦通过谨慎的分阶段再喂养可以逆转,身高别体重可恢复。若病程发生在生命最初1000天内,则不能完全恢复的是线性生长和神经认知发育:两岁前形成的生长迟缓大多为永久性的,相关的认知缺陷会持续到成年。肌少症部分可逆,充足蛋白质配合抗阻训练可重建力量和部分肌肉量,但数十年间流失的肌肉无法完全恢复。
items.at_risk_zh: 处于食物不安全环境中的儿童,尤其是断奶前后及感染之后。住院患者、术后患者和重症患者。食欲不振、牙齿问题、吞咽困难或社会孤立的老年人。存在吸收不良、肝硬化,或因癌症、晚期肾衰竭或心力衰竭而恶病质的人。神经性厌食症患者。富裕国家中摄入充足热量的健康成年人几乎不会出现蛋白质不足。
items.prevalence_zh: 2024年,5岁以下儿童中有4280万人消瘦(6.6%),其中1220万人为重度消瘦(1.9%),另有1.502亿人生长迟缓(联合国儿童基金会/世界卫生组织/世界银行联合营养不良估计,2025年版)。老年人肌少症的合并患病率在EWGSOP1标准下为17.7%,在EWGSOP2标准下为11%,各研究间的范围分别为6.2%至35.3%和3.2%至26.3%(Fernandes LV等,Aging Clin Exp Res. 2022;34:505-514)。

items.function_short_zh: 一种人体自身可以合成的氨基酸,是肠壁和免疫细胞偏好使用的燃料。
items.function_full_zh: 谷氨酰胺是血浆和骨骼肌中含量最丰富的游离氨基酸。肌肉通过glutamine synthetase持续合成并输出谷氨酰胺,因此其供给通常由内源性生成决定,而非由饮食决定。肠上皮细胞和快速分裂的免疫细胞将其作为首选的呼吸燃料,并作为嘌呤、嘧啶和谷胱甘肽合成的氮供体,这正是肠道修复说法背后的生化基础。健康状态下它被归为非必需氨基酸,在严重分解代谢状态下(此时肌肉输出跟不上消耗)则为条件必需氨基酸。关于口服谷氨酰胺用于肠道通透性、肠易激综合征和炎症性肠病的人体试验规模小且结果不一致,最强的证据出现在特定临床情境中,而非健康人群中。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 不适用。谷氨酰胺没有膳食需求量,因此不存在可检测的膳食性缺乏。血浆谷氨酰胺降低是重症、重大创伤或烧伤的后果,而不是饮食造成的。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 不适用。在80例非择期入院患者中,ICU入院时血浆谷氨酰胺低于0.420 mmol/L与更高的死亡率相关(Oudemans-van Straaten HM等,PMID 11280678),但这标志的是分解代谢的严重程度,而非营养素缺乏。将其当作需要纠正的缺乏来治疗被证明是有害的:在纳入1223例伴多器官衰竭的机械通气ICU患者的REDOXS试验中,大剂量谷氨酰胺增加了住院期间及六个月死亡率(PMID 23594003)。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 不适用。不存在需要逆转的谷氨酰胺缺乏。
items.at_risk_zh: 不适用。没有人会因饮食而缺乏谷氨酰胺。血浆浓度降低见于脓毒症、重度烧伤、重大创伤和长期重症,反映的是原发疾病本身。

items.function_short_zh: 作为蛋白质摄入的水解动物胶原蛋白,而人体自身的胶原蛋白是由普通氨基酸构建的。
items.function_full_zh: 胶原蛋白是人体中含量最丰富的蛋白质,约占全身蛋白质总量的三分之一,构成皮肤、肌腱、韧带、骨基质、软骨和血管壁的抗张骨架。人体由普通氨基酸合成胶原蛋白,形成富含脯氨酸的重复Gly-X-Y序列,稳定三螺旋结构的翻译后羟基化由prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases完成,该过程需要维生素C、铁和2-氧戊二酸。摄入的胶原蛋白像其他蛋白质一样被消化,不过部分二肽和三肽,如脯氨酰羟脯氨酸,确实能完整进入血液,这被提出作为超出单纯氨基酸供给之外任何效应的机制。作为蛋白质来源,胶原蛋白在营养上并不完整:它不含色氨酸,其他几种必需氨基酸含量也偏低。
items.deficiency_name_zh: 无。坏血病有时被笼统地描述为胶原蛋白缺乏,这是一种误读:它实际上是维生素C缺乏,而胶原蛋白的缺陷是缺少酶辅因子的下游结果。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 不适用。胶原蛋白不是膳食必需营养素,不存在膳食性胶原蛋白缺乏。胶原蛋白真正的功能障碍来自维生素C缺乏(坏血病)、胶原蛋白基因的遗传缺陷(osteogenesis imperfecta、Ehlers-Danlos综合征各型),或整体蛋白质能量营养不良。以上情况都不能通过摄入胶原蛋白来纠正。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 不适用。不存在需要逆转的膳食性胶原蛋白缺乏。
items.at_risk_zh: 不适用。有一个理论上的论点值得提及,但不宜夸大:一项化学计量学分析计算得出,内源性甘氨酸合成加上典型膳食甘氨酸摄入量,比70 kg成年人实现最大胶原蛋白周转所需的量约低10 g/day(PMID 20093739)。这仍只是一项计算结果,临床上尚未证实存在甘氨酸或胶原蛋白缺乏状态。

items.function_short_zh: 一种成胶纤维,能在粪便中保留水分,使其更软、更蓬松、更易排出。
items.function_full_zh: 车前子壳是卵叶车前(Plantago ovata)碾磨后的种皮,主要成分是高度支化的阿拉伯木聚糖,具有成胶特性,而且不同于大多数黏性纤维,它很少被结肠细菌发酵。由于它能完整到达直肠,水分得以在那里保留,形成蓬松柔软的粪便,产气也远少于可发酵纤维。它能双向调节粪便性状,使干硬粪便变软,使稀软粪便成形。同样的凝胶还会提高小肠内容物的黏度,减慢葡萄糖吸收并结合胆汁酸,由此造成的胆汁酸流失促使肝脏以胆固醇为原料加速合成,从而降低LDL。在肠易激综合征(IBS)中,车前子壳是真正有试验支持的纤维:洋车前子使IBS未改善的相对风险为0.83(95% CI 0.73至0.94),需治疗人数(NNT)为7(95% CI 4至25),是ACG指南推荐使用的纤维(PMID 33315591)。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 不适用。不存在车前子壳缺乏症,车前子壳只是纠正膳食总纤维不足的一种方式,而这种不足属于总纤维的问题,总纤维在本组中没有独立词条。低纤维摄入最先表现为粪便更硬、排便次数减少、排便费力、全肠道转运时间延长和粪便重量减轻。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 不适用。低纤维摄入同样不会导致某种缺乏病。现有证据支持的是一种梯度关联:汇总185项前瞻性研究和58项试验后,纤维摄入最高组的全因死亡率和心血管死亡率比最低组低15%至30%,冠心病、卒中、2型糖尿病和结直肠癌的发病率也更低。风险下降幅度最大出现在25至29 g/day区间,剂量反应曲线提示(但未证实)30 g/day以上可能有额外获益(Reynolds等,PMID 30638909)。未经治疗的慢性便秘本身可能进展为粪便嵌塞,极少数情况下发生粪性溃疡或穿孔。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 不适用。不存在需要逆转的车前子壳缺乏。服用后的效果属于药效学范畴:粪便性状、排便频率、转运时间以及LDL和餐后血糖的变化,在充分摄入数天至几周内即可改善,停用后又会恢复原状。死亡率和癌症方面的关联与长期饮食模式有关,而非短期补充,也没有任何试验证明纤维补充剂能逆转已形成的结直肠肿瘤。
items.at_risk_zh: 作为缺乏症不适用。就总纤维摄入不足而言:大多数采用西式饮食的人,尤其是主要吃精制谷物、蔬菜豆类水果摄入很少的人,以及长期采用低渣或限制性饮食的人。美国成年人平均摄入量约为16 g/day,而适宜摄入量对年轻女性为25 g/day,对年轻男性为38 g/day。
items.prevalence_zh: 不适用。车前子壳没有设定需求量,因此没有相应的达标率数据。就膳食总纤维而言,美国人群中约5%达到适宜摄入量(Quagliani D, Felt-Gunderson P. Am J Lifestyle Med. 2017;11:80-85),7.4%的美国成年人达到每1000 kcal 14 g的标准(Miketinas DC等,常规纤维摄入量,NHANES 2013-2018);美国成年人平均摄入量约为16 g/day(WWEIA NHANES 2009-2010,NCBI Bookshelf NBK589559)。

items.supplement_zh: 益生元:菊粉、低聚果糖(FOS)、低聚半乳糖(GOS)
items.function_short_zh: 肠道细菌的食物来源纤维,可增加双歧杆菌数量,并在结肠中产生短链脂肪酸。
items.function_full_zh: 菊粉和低聚果糖是来自菊苣根、菊芋、洋葱、大蒜和小麦的果糖聚合物,两者主要区别在于链长:FOS的聚合度低于约9,菊粉可延伸到60。GOS是由乳糖经酶促反应生成的半乳糖寡糖,是人乳低聚糖的结构类似物。这三者都能抵抗人体消化酶,完整到达结肠并被选择性发酵,可重复性地提高双歧杆菌丰度,这也是ISAPP将益生元定义为被宿主微生物选择性利用、能带来健康益处的底物这一定义的依据(PMID 28611480)。发酵产生乙酸、丙酸和丁酸,丁酸是结肠上皮细胞的主要呼吸燃料,短链脂肪酸池能降低肠腔pH并支持屏障功能。正是这种可发酵性也造成了这些化合物以产气和腹胀著称,因而被归为高FODMAP食物。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 不适用。不存在益生元特有的缺乏症,也没有设定需求量。可发酵底物摄入不足会降低结肠短链脂肪酸的生成,尤其是丁酸,并减少双歧杆菌丰度。这两者都可在粪便中测得,但都不会产生本人能察觉的症状,而且两者都是对摄入量的药效学反应,而不是缺乏状态。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 不适用。人体不存在严重的缺乏综合征。最有力的机制性发现来自小鼠:在慢性或间歇性纤维剥夺状态下,肠道菌群转而降解宿主分泌的黏液糖蛋白,使结肠黏液屏障变薄,增加对肠道病原体的易感性(Desai等,PMID 27863247)。这一发现尚未被证明会在人体中导致疾病,归因于低纤维摄入的人体结局最好在总纤维层面而非益生元特异性层面评估。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 不适用。不存在需要逆转的益生元缺乏。服用后的反应属于药效学范畴:双歧杆菌丰度和短链脂肪酸产量在摄入后数天至约一周内上升,停用后经过类似的时间又会回到基线附近。这种效应始终依赖于摄入量,补充停止后不会有持久的菌群组成改变留存。
items.at_risk_zh: 作为缺乏症不适用。从摄入角度看,洋葱、大蒜、韭葱、菊苣、小麦、香蕉或豆类摄入量少的人摄入量偏低。为治疗IBS而采用低FODMAP饮食的人恰好限制了这些底物,可测得双歧杆菌显著下降,这也是限制阶段应设定为限时、并在之后进行有计划再引入的原因。使用未添加GOS或FOS配方奶的婴儿则完全没有摄入。
items.prevalence_zh: 不适用。益生元没有设定需求量,因此没有达标率数据。欧洲和美国人群习惯性菊粉型果聚糖摄入量估计约为1至10 g/day。

items.supplement: Wheat bran and insoluble fibre supplements for IBS
items.supplement_zh: 小麦麸皮及IBS用不溶性纤维补充剂
items.function_short_zh: 一种粗糙的不溶性纤维,通过机械作用增加粪便体积,在IBS患者中常使症状加重。
items.function_full_zh: 小麦麸皮是小麦籽粒的外层,主要由不溶性阿拉伯木聚糖、纤维素和木质素组成。它的作用方式是颗粒体积和对黏膜的机械刺激,而不是成胶:粗颗粒能增加粪便质量并促进分泌和蠕动,而磨得很细的麸皮会失去这种效果,甚至可能减慢转运。它保水能力远低于车前子壳,且部分被发酵而产气。在IBS患者中,这些特性反而不利,因为机械刺激作用于本已过度敏感的肠道,而且麸皮还含有果聚糖,属于高FODMAP食物。荟萃分析未发现麸皮对IBS整体症状有显著获益(未改善的相对风险为0.90,95% CI 0.79至1.03),与洋车前子(NNT为7)形成对比,ACG指南推荐IBS患者使用可溶性纤维(PMID 33315591)。
items.deficiency_early_zh: 不适用。不存在小麦麸皮缺乏症。麸皮是作为补充剂出售的一种食物成分,而非营养素,值得描述的不足属于膳食总纤维:摄入不足会导致粪便更硬、排便次数减少、排便费力、粪便重量减轻和全肠道转运减慢。对于麸皮曾是唯一纤维来源的人,停用麸皮会重现这些表现。
items.deficiency_severe_zh: 不适用。不服用麸皮补充剂不会带来任何严重后果。一般性的低纤维关联依然适用:总纤维摄入最高组比最低组的全因死亡率和心血管死亡率低15%至30%,冠心病、卒中、2型糖尿病和结直肠癌发病率也更低(PMID 30638909)。而在IBS患者中,更常见的临床问题恰恰相反。在100例连续转诊、尝试过麸皮的IBS患者中,55%报告症状因此加重,只有10%认为有帮助,肠道功能紊乱、腹胀和腹痛均被加重(Francis和Whorwell,PMID 7912305)。
items.reversibility_note_zh: 不适用。不存在需要逆转的麸皮缺乏。服用或停用麸皮引起的变化属于药效学范畴:改变不溶性纤维摄入后,粪便体积、排便频率和转运时间在数天内即有反应,停用后又会恢复,麸皮诱发的IBS症状加重在停用麸皮后即可缓解,未见描述有持久的黏膜或功能损害。
items.at_risk_zh: 作为缺乏症不适用。就总纤维摄入不足而言:主要食用精制谷物、植物性食物摄入很少的人,美国成年人平均摄入量约为16 g/day,而适宜摄入量为25至38 g/day。就危害而非不足而言:IBS患者是最可能被建议食用麸皮、也最可能因此症状加重的人群。
items.prevalence_zh: 不适用。麸皮没有设定需求量,因此没有达标率数据。就膳食总纤维而言,美国人群中约5%达到适宜摄入量(Quagliani D, Felt-Gunderson P. Am J Lifestyle Med. 2017;11:80-85),美国成年人平均摄入量约为16 g/day(WWEIA NHANES 2009-2010,NCBI Bookshelf NBK589559)。就IBS患者对麸皮的不耐受而言,100例连续转诊的IBS患者中有55%报告麸皮使症状加重(PMID 7912305)。

items.function_short: Recycles ATP inside muscle and brain cells, buffering energy during short bursts of intense effort.
items.function_full: Creatine is phosphorylated by creatine kinase to phosphocreatine, a rapid-turnover phosphate reservoir that regenerates ATP from ADP during high-intensity contraction and in neurons. Roughly half of the daily turnover (about 1 to 3 g) is synthesized endogenously from arginine, glycine and methionine by AGAT and GAMT in liver, kidney and pancreas; the remainder comes from meat and fish. There is no dietary requirement. Vegetarians carry intramuscular creatine roughly 10 to 15 percent below omnivores and remain healthy, they simply respond more strongly to supplementation. That range comes from two different designs: Blancquaert et al. 2018 is an intervention trial in 40 omnivorous women in which vastus lateralis total creatine fell 15 percent over 3 months in the vegetarian-plus-placebo arm (against +9.7 percent vegetarian-plus-creatine and +6.8 percent omnivorous control), while cross-sectional comparisons of habitual vegetarians report a smaller gap of around 10 percent. Separately from anything to do with intake, three inborn errors of metabolism produce the cerebral creatine deficiency syndromes: GAMT deficiency, AGAT deficiency and X-linked creatine transporter (SLC6A8) deficiency. These are genetic defects of synthesis or transport, not consequences of eating too little creatine, and no dietary pattern produces them. Onset is in infancy or early childhood with global developmental delay, expressive speech delay out of proportion to other skills and hypotonia, plus early epilepsy and a movement disorder in GAMT deficiency; brain magnetic resonance spectroscopy showing an absent or near-absent creatine peak is the diagnostic finding. Untreated GAMT deficiency causes intractable seizures, autistic features, extrapyramidal movement disorder and severe intellectual disability, with accumulated guanidinoacetate contributing to the neurotoxicity, and creatine transporter deficiency causes lifelong moderate to severe intellectual disability and seizures in affected males. AGAT and GAMT deficiency respond to oral creatine (with arginine restriction and ornithine in GAMT), and 7 of 8 infants treated before 6 months of age had normal developmental outcomes, which is what makes early detection decisive; creatine transporter deficiency does not respond to oral creatine at all, because the transporter that would carry it into the brain is the broken protein. On frequency, GeneReviews gives an estimated GAMT incidence of 1:2,640,000 to 1:250,000; prospective newborn screening in Utah and New York found 1:405,655; a single-centre referral series of 5 patients seen between 2001 and 2011 produced a much higher outlier estimate of 1:114,000. Creatine transporter deficiency is reported in 0.4 to 1.4 percent of cohorts of males with intellectual disability, and separately in 2.64 percent of a more recent cohort of individuals with neurodevelopmental disorders that was neither male-restricted nor restricted to intellectual disability of unknown cause.
items.source: GeneReviews, Creatine Deficiency Disorders, NCBI Bookshelf NBK3794; PMID 29569535 (Blancquaert et al., Br J Nutr 2018;119(7):759-770, 3-month vegetarian diet intervention in 40 omnivorous women); Burke et al., Med Sci Sports Exerc 2003 (cross-sectional vegetarian versus omnivore muscle creatine); Pediatrics 2023;152(2):e2023062100, PMID 37465909 (newborn screening evidence review)
corrections_applied: deficiency_state CLINICAL to NONE per misclassified: creatine is not an essential nutrient and every basis for the CLINICAL label was an inborn error of metabolism (GATM, GAMT, SLC6A8); follows the alpha-lipoic acid template already in the dataset

items.function_short: The raw material for carnosine, which buffers acid build-up in muscle during hard efforts.
items.function_full: Beta-alanine is the rate-limiting substrate for carnosine synthase, which joins it to histidine to form carnosine in skeletal muscle. Carnosine acts as an intracellular pH buffer across the physiological range and also chelates metals and scavenges reactive carbonyls. Supplementation raises muscle carnosine by up to 64 percent at 4 weeks and up to 80 percent at 10 weeks, and produces a small performance gain concentrated in efforts of roughly 0.5 to 10 minutes, with no benefit below 30 seconds and only a non-significant moderate effect beyond 10 minutes (Saunders et al. 2017, 40 studies, 1,461 subjects); the ISSN position stand places the most pronounced benefit in open end-point tasks and time trials lasting 1 to 4 minutes. The body forms beta-alanine from uracil degradation in the liver and also obtains it from meat-derived carnosine and anserine. It is a non-essential amino acid with no recommended intake.
items.source: PMID 26175657 (Trexler et al., International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand: beta-alanine, J Int Soc Sports Nutr 2015, PMC4501114); Saunders et al., Br J Sports Med 2017;51:658-669
corrections_applied: function_full: performance window 'about 30 seconds to 10 minutes' re-attributed to its actual source, Saunders et al. 2017 (0.5 to 10 min, no benefit below 30 s, non-significant beyond 10 min), and the ISSN stand's own 1 to 4 minute framing stated alongside it

function_full: carnosine increase 'roughly 40 to 80 percent' replaced with the figures the cited ISSN stand actually reports, up to 64 percent at 4 weeks and up to 80 percent at 10 weeks; the unsupported 40 percent floor removed
